title.zh: 卷一百六十一 列傳第一百十一: 李光進 烏重胤 王沛 李珙 李祐 董重質 楊元卿 劉悟 劉沔 石雄
title.en: Volume 161 Biographies 111: Li Guangjin, Wu Zhongyin, Wang Pei, Li Gong, Li You, Dong Zhongzhi, Yang Yuanqing, Liu Wu, Liu Mian, Shi Xiong
title.raw: 卷一百六十一 列傳第一百十一: 李光進 烏重胤 王沛 李珙 李祐 董重質 楊元卿 劉悟 劉沔 石雄 Volume 161 Biographies 111: Li Guangjin, Wu Zhongyin, Wang Pei, Li Gong, Li You, Dong Zhongzhi, Yang Yuanqing, Liu Wu, Liu Mian, Shi Xiong

sentences.zh: 李光進，本河曲部落稽阿跌之族也。

translations.literal: Li Guangjin was originally of the Jie'adie clan among the Hequ tribal groups.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangjin came from the Jie'adie people of the Hequ tribes.

sentences.zh: 父良臣，襲雞田州刺史，隸朔方軍。

translations.literal: His father Liangchen inherited the post of Governor of Jitian Prefecture and was attached to the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liangchen succeeded to the governorship of Jitian Prefecture and served under the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 光進姊適舍利葛旃，殺僕固瑒而事河東節度使辛雲京。

translations.literal: Guangjin's elder sister married Sheli Gezhan, who killed Pugu Chang and submitted to Hedong Military Governor Xin Yunjing.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin's sister married Sheli Gezhan, who slew Pugu Chang and went over to Hedong governor Xin Yunjing.

sentences.zh: 光進兄弟少依葛旃，因家於太原。

translations.literal: Guangjin and his brothers depended on Gezhan in their youth, and thus made their home in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangjin brothers were raised under Gezhan's care and settled their household in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 光進勇毅果敢，其武藝兵略次於葛旃。

translations.literal: Guangjin was courageous, resolute, and bold; in martial skill and military strategy he was second only to Gezhan.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin was brave and decisive; only Gezhan surpassed him in arms and strategy.

sentences.zh: 肅宗自靈武觀兵，光進從郭子儀破賊，收兩京，累有戰功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reviewed the troops at Lingwu, Guangjin followed Guo Ziyi in defeating the rebels, recovering the two capitals, and accumulated repeated battle merits.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong inspected the army at Lingwu, Guangjin followed Guo Ziyi against the rebels, helped recover the two capitals, and won distinction again and again.

sentences.zh: 至德中，授代州刺史，封范陽郡公，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the Zhide era he was appointed Governor of Daizhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhide he was made governor of Daizhou and enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上元初，郭子儀為朔方節度，以軍討大同、橫野、清夷，范陽及河北殘寇，用光進為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Early in the Shangyuan era, Guo Ziyi was Military Governor of Shuofang and led troops against the remnants at Datong, Hengye, Qingyi, Fanyang, and Hebei; Guangjin was made Chief Controller of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shangyuan, as Guo Ziyi campaigned from Shuofang against rebel holdouts in Datong, Hengye, Qingyi, Fanyang, and Hebei, Guangjin was appointed chief controller of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋遷渭北節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was transferred to Military Governor of Weibei.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to military governor of Weibei.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，進封武威郡王。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongtai era, he was advanced to Prince of Wuwei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongtai he was promoted to Prince of Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 大歷四年，檢校戶部尚書，知省事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dali, he was made Acting Minister of Revenue with charge of routine matters at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dali he was made acting minister of revenue with charge of routine Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又轉檢校刑部尚書、兼太子太保。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Acting Minister of Justice and concurrent Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to acting minister of justice and concurrent grand mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 是歲冬十月，葬母於京城之南原，將相致祭者凡四十四幄，窮極奢靡，城內士庶，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: That winter in the tenth month he buried his mother on the southern plateau outside the capital; ministers and generals who came to offer sacrifices set up forty-four pavilions, with luxury carried to extremes, and city folk and commoners watched in crowds thick as a wall.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the tenth month, he buried his mother on the southern plateau outside the capital. Ministers and generals who came to sacrifice pitched forty-four tents, with extravagance pushed to the limit, while townsfolk and commoners watched in a throng that blocked the streets.

sentences.zh: 元和四年，王承宗反。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Wang Chengzong rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhe, Wang Chengzong rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 范希朝引師救易定，表光進為步都虞候，戰於木刀溝，光進有功。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao led troops to relieve Yiding and recommended Guangjin as Infantry Chief Commandant; at the battle of Mudao Gully Guangjin distinguished himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao marched to relieve Yiding, recommended Guangjin as infantry chief commandant, and at Mudao Gully Guangjin won credit.

sentences.zh: 六年，拜銀青光祿大夫、檢校工部尚書，充單於大都護、振武節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Silver-Cyan Grand Guardian of the Imperial Park, Acting Minister of Works, Grand Protector-General of the Xiongnu, and Military Governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed silver-cyan grand guardian of the imperial park, acting minister of works, grand protector-general of the Xiongnu, and military governor of Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 詔以光進夙有誠節，克著茂勛，賜姓李氏。

translations.literal: An edict noted that Guangjin had long shown loyalty and integrity and had achieved splendid merit, and bestowed on him the surname Li.
translations.idiomatic: An edict cited Guangjin's long-standing loyalty and splendid achievements and granted him the surname Li.

sentences.zh: 其弟光顏除洺州刺史，充本州團練使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guangyan was appointed Governor of Mingzhou and Military Training Commissioner of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Guangyan was appointed governor of Mingzhou and military training commissioner of that prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄弟恩澤同時，人皆嘆異。

translations.literal: The brothers received imperial favor at the same time, and all marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers received imperial favor at the same time, and everyone marveled at it.

sentences.zh: 八年，遷靈武節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Military Governor of Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to military governor of Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 光進嘗從馬燧救臨洺，戰洹水，收河中，皆有功。

translations.literal: Guangjin had once followed Ma Sui in relieving Linming, fighting at the Huan River, and recovering the Hezhong region, distinguishing himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin had followed Ma Sui to relieve Linming, fought at the Huan River, and helped recover Hezhong, distinguishing himself each time.

sentences.zh: 前後軍中之職，無所不歷；

translations.literal: Over the years he held every military post there was;
translations.idiomatic: Over the years he had held every military post in the army;

sentences.zh: 中丞、大夫悉曾兼帶。

translations.literal: and had held every combination of Censor-in-Chief and Grandee titles.
translations.idiomatic: and had held every combination of censor-in-chief and grandee titles as well.

sentences.zh: 先是救易定之師，光進、光顏皆在其行，故軍中呼光進為大大夫，光顏為小大夫。

translations.literal: Earlier, on the expedition to relieve Yiding, both Guangjin and Guangyan were in the column, so the army called Guangjin "Elder Grandee" and Guangyan "Younger Grandee."
translations.idiomatic: On the earlier expedition to relieve Yiding, both Guangjin and Guangyan had marched in the same force, so the troops called Guangjin "Elder Grandee" and Guangyan "Younger Grandee."

sentences.zh: 十年七月卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the tenth year.

sentences.zh: 光進兄弟少以孝睦推於軍中。

translations.literal: The Guangjin brothers were known in the army from youth for filial piety and harmonious conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the Guangjin brothers were esteemed in the army for filial devotion and brotherly harmony.

sentences.zh: 及居母喪，三年不歸寢室。

translations.literal: During their mother's mourning they did not return to the marital bedchamber for three years.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning their mother, they did not enter the marital bedchamber for three years.

sentences.zh: 光顏先娶妻，其母委以家事。

translations.literal: Guangyan had married first, and their mother entrusted household affairs to his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had married first, and their mother put him in charge of the household through his wife.

sentences.zh: 母卒，光進始娶。

translations.literal: When their mother died, Guangjin married for the first time.
translations.idiomatic: Only after their mother died did Guangjin marry.

sentences.zh: 光顏使其妻奉管籥、家籍、財物，歸於其姒。

translations.literal: Guangyan had his wife surrender the keys, household registers, and property to their elder sister-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had his wife hand over the keys, household registers, and property to their elder sister-in-law.

sentences.zh: 光進命反之，且謂光顏曰：「新婦逮事母，嘗命以主家，不可改也。」

translations.literal: Guangjin ordered this reversed and said to Guangyan: "Your wife served our mother from the start and was charged with managing the household—that must not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Guangjin ordered this reversed and told Guangyan, "Your wife served our mother from the first and was charged with running the household. That cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 因相持泣良久，乃如初。

translations.literal: They embraced and wept together for a long time, then matters returned as before.
translations.idiomatic: They embraced and wept together for a long time, and afterward everything was as before.

sentences.zh: 卒時年六十五，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously made left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 光顏與兄光進以葛旃善騎射，兄弟自幼皆師之，葛旃獨許光顏之勇健，己不能逮。

translations.literal: Guangyan and his elder brother Guangjin took Gezhan as their master because he excelled at mounted archery; from childhood both brothers studied under him, and Gezhan singled out Guangyan's valor and vigor as surpassing his own.
translations.idiomatic: Because Gezhan excelled at mounted archery, Guangyan and his elder brother Guangjin had studied under him from childhood. Gezhan alone acknowledged that Guangyan's courage and strength exceeded his own.

sentences.zh: 及長，從河東軍為裨將，討李懷光、楊惠琳，皆有功。

translations.literal: When grown he served in the Hedong army as a deputy commander and took part in campaigns against Li Huiguang and Yang Huilin, distinguishing himself in each.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he served in the Hedong army as a deputy commander and distinguished himself in campaigns against Li Huiguang and Yang Huilin.

sentences.zh: 後隨高崇文平蜀，搴旗斬將，出入如神，由是稍稍知名。

translations.literal: Later he followed Gao Chongwen in pacifying Shu, seizing enemy banners and slaying generals, advancing and retreating like a spirit, and from this gradually won renown.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Gao Chongwen in pacifying Shu, seizing banners and slaying enemy generals, moving through the battle lines like a spirit, and from this gradually won fame.

sentences.zh: 自憲宗元和已來，歷授代、洺二州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Since Emperor Xianzong's Yuanhe era he had successively been appointed Governor of Dai and Ming prefectures, concurrently serving as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianzong's Yuanhe reign he had successively been appointed governor of Dai and Ming prefectures, concurrently serving as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 九年，將討淮、蔡，九月，遷陳州刺史，充忠武軍都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when a campaign against Huai and Cai was planned, in the ninth month he was transferred to Governor of Chenzhou and Chief Controller of Military Affairs of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, as a campaign against Huai and Cai was planned, in the ninth month he was transferred to governor of Chenzhou and chief controller of military affairs for the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 逾月，遷忠武軍節度使、檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: A month later he was made Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army and Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made military governor of the Zhongwu Army and acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷征天下兵，環申、蔡而討吳元濟，詔光顏以本軍獨當一面。

translations.literal: The court summoned armies from throughout the realm to encircle Shen and Cai and campaign against Wu Yuanji; Guangyan was ordered to hold one front alone with his own army.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned armies from throughout the realm to surround Shen and Cai and campaign against Wu Yuanji, and Guangyan was ordered to hold one front alone with his own army.

sentences.zh: 光顏於是引兵臨溵水，抗洄曲。

translations.literal: Guangyan thereupon led his troops to the Yin River and confronted the enemy at Huaiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan thereupon led his troops to the Yin River and confronted the rebels at Huaiqu.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，破元濟之師於時曲。

translations.literal: The next year in the fifth month he defeated Yuanji's army at Shiqu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, in the fifth month, he defeated Yuanji's army at Shiqu.

sentences.zh: 初，賊眾晨壓光顏之壘而陣，光顏不得出，乃自毀其柵之左右，出騎以突之。

translations.literal: At first the rebel host pressed Guangyan's camp at dawn and formed battle lines; unable to sally forth, he had the palisades on his flanks torn down and led cavalry in a charge against them.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rebels pressed Guangyan's camp at dawn and formed their lines. Unable to break out, he had the palisades on his flanks torn down and led cavalry in a charge against them.

sentences.zh: 光顏將數騎冒堅而沖之，出入者數四。

translations.literal: Guangyan led a few horsemen straight through the enemy lines, charging in and out four times.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan led a few horsemen straight through the enemy lines, charging in and out four times.

sentences.zh: 賊眾盡識，矢集於身如蝟。

translations.literal: The rebels all recognized him; arrows clustered on his body like a hedgehog.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all recognized him, and arrows clustered on his body like quills on a hedgehog.

sentences.zh: 其子攬光顏馬鞅，止其深入。

translations.literal: His son seized Guangyan's horse's crupper and stopped him from pressing deeper in.
translations.idiomatic: His son seized the crupper of Guangyan's horse and stopped him from driving deeper into the enemy.

sentences.zh: 光顏舉刃叱之，乃退。

translations.literal: Guangyan raised his blade and shouted at him, and only then did he withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan raised his blade and shouted him down, and only then did he withdraw.

sentences.zh: 於是人爭奮躍。

translations.literal: At this everyone strove forward with renewed zeal.
translations.idiomatic: At this the men all strove forward with renewed zeal.

sentences.zh: 賊乃大潰，死者數千人。

translations.literal: The rebels routed in great disorder, and several thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and fled in disorder, and several thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 捷聲至京師，人人相賀。

translations.literal: News of victory reached the capital and everyone congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: News of the victory reached the capital, and everyone congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 時伐蔡之師，大小凡十余鎮，自裴度使還，唯奏光顏勇而知義，終不辱命。

translations.literal: At the time the armies campaigning against Cai numbered more than a dozen commands large and small; after Pei Du returned from his assignment, he reported only that Guangyan was brave and understood righteousness and would never disgrace his commission.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the armies campaigning against Cai numbered more than a dozen commands large and small. After Pei Du returned from his mission, he reported only that Guangyan was brave, understood righteousness, and would never fail his charge.

sentences.zh: 至是，果立功焉。

translations.literal: On this occasion he indeed achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he indeed won distinction.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月，光顏又與懷汝節度烏重胤同破元濟之眾於小溵河，平其柵。

translations.literal: That eleventh month Guangyan joined Wu Zhongyin, Military Governor of Huairu, in defeating Yuanji's forces on the Xiao Yin River and leveling their stockade.
translations.idiomatic: That eleventh month Guangyan joined Huairu governor Wu Zhongyin in defeating Yuanji's forces on the Xiao Yin River and leveling their stockade.

sentences.zh: 初，都統韓弘令諸軍齊攻賊城，賊又徑攻烏重胤之壘。

translations.literal: At first Supreme Commander Han Hong ordered all armies to attack the rebel city together, but the rebels then struck directly at Wu Zhongyin's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At first supreme commander Han Hong ordered all the armies to attack the rebel city together, but the rebels then struck directly at Wu Zhongyin's camp.

sentences.zh: 重胤禦之，中數槍，馳請救於光顏。

translations.literal: Zhongyin defended against them, was struck by several spears, and galloped to Guangyan to beg for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyin held them off, was struck by several spears, and galloped to Guangyan to beg for relief.

sentences.zh: 光顏以小溵橋賊之堡也，乘其無備，使田穎、宋朝隱襲而取之。

translations.literal: Guangyan knew that the Xiao Yin bridge was the rebels' strongpoint; taking advantage of their unpreparedness, he sent Tian Ying and Song Chaoyin to raid and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan knew the Xiao Yin bridge was the rebels' strongpoint. Taking advantage of their unpreparedness, he sent Tian Ying and Song Chaoyin to raid and seize it.

sentences.zh: 乃平其城塹，由是克救重胤。

translations.literal: He then leveled their walls and moats, and in this way was able to rescue Zhongyin.
translations.idiomatic: He then leveled their walls and moats, and in this way was able to rescue Zhongyin.

sentences.zh: 韓弘以光顏違令，取穎及朝隱將戮之。

translations.literal: Han Hong, on the grounds that Guangyan had disobeyed orders, seized Ying and Chaoyin and was about to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong, on the grounds that Guangyan had disobeyed orders, seized Ying and Chaoyin and was about to execute them.

sentences.zh: 穎及朝隱勇而材，軍中皆惋惜之。

translations.literal: Ying and Chaoyin were brave and talented, and everyone in the army regretted their fate.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Chaoyin were brave and talented, and everyone in the army regretted their fate.

sentences.zh: 光顏畏弘不敢留。

translations.literal: Guangyan feared Hong and did not dare keep them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan feared Hong and did not dare keep them.

sentences.zh: 會中使景忠信至，知其情，乃矯詔令所在械系之。

translations.literal: When the palace envoy Jing Zhongxin arrived and learned the situation, he forged an edict ordering that they be shackled wherever found.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace envoy Jing Zhongxin arrived and learned the situation, he forged an edict ordering that they be shackled wherever found.

sentences.zh: 走馬入見，具以本末聞。

translations.literal: He galloped in to an audience and reported the whole course of events.
translations.idiomatic: He galloped in to an audience and reported the whole course of events.

sentences.zh: 憲宗赦忠信矯詔罪，令即往釋穎及朝隱。

translations.literal: Xianzong pardoned Zhongxin for forging the edict and ordered him to go at once and release Ying and Chaoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong pardoned Zhongxin for forging the edict and ordered him to go at once and release Ying and Chaoyin.

sentences.zh: 弘及光顏叠以表論。

translations.literal: Hong and Guangyan submitted memorial after memorial arguing the case.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and Guangyan submitted memorial after memorial arguing the case.

sentences.zh: 憲宗謂弘使曰：「穎等違都統令，固當處死。

translations.literal: Xianzong said to Hong's envoy: "Ying and the others disobeyed the supreme commander's orders and certainly ought to be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong told Hong's envoy, "Ying and the others disobeyed the supreme commander's orders and certainly ought to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 但光顏以其襲賊有功，亦可宥之。

translations.literal: But because Guangyan's raid on the rebels achieved merit, they may also be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: But because Guangyan's raid on the rebels achieved merit, they may also be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 軍有三令五申，宜舍此以收來效。」

translations.literal: The army has its repeated commands and prohibitions; it is fitting to set this aside in order to win future service."
translations.idiomatic: The army has its repeated commands and prohibitions. It is fitting to set this aside in order to win future service."

sentences.zh: 及以詔諭弘，弘不悅。

translations.literal: When the edict was conveyed to Hong, he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was conveyed to Hong, he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 十一年，光顏連敗元濟之眾，拔賊淩雲柵，憲宗大悅，賜其告捷者奴婢銀錦。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Guangyan repeatedly defeated Yuanji's forces and captured the rebels' Lingyun stockade; Xianzong was greatly pleased and rewarded the bearer of the victory report with slaves, silver, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangyan repeatedly defeated Yuanji's forces and captured the rebels' Lingyun stockade. Xianzong was greatly pleased and rewarded the bearer of the victory report with slaves, silver, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 進位檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，光顏敗元濟之眾三萬於郾城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twelfth year Guangyan defeated thirty thousand of Yuanji's troops at Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the twelfth year Guangyan defeated thirty thousand of Yuanji's troops at Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 其將張伯良奔於蔡州，殺其賊什二三，獲馬千匹，器甲三萬聯，皆畫雷公符。

translations.literal: His general Zhang Boliang fled to Caizhou, killing two or three tenths of the rebels; they captured a thousand horses and thirty thousand sets of armor and weapons, all painted with the Thunder Lord talisman.
translations.idiomatic: His general Zhang Boliang fled to Caizhou, killing two or three tenths of the rebels. They captured a thousand horses and thirty thousand sets of armor and weapons, all painted with the Thunder Lord talisman.

sentences.zh: 仍書云：「速破城北軍。」

translations.literal: They also bore an inscription reading: "Quickly break the army north of the city."
translations.idiomatic: They also bore an inscription reading, "Quickly break the army north of the city."

sentences.zh: 尋而郾城守將鄧懷金請以城降。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter Yancheng's defending general Deng Huaijin asked to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly thereafter Yancheng's defending general Deng Huaijin asked to surrender the city.

sentences.zh: 光顏許之，而收郾城。

translations.literal: Guangyan agreed and took possession of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan agreed and took possession of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 初，鄧懷金以官軍圍青陵城，絕其歸路，懷金懼，謀於郾城令董昌齡。

translations.literal: At first Deng Huaijin, with government troops besieging Qingling and cutting off his line of retreat, was afraid and consulted Yancheng magistrate Dong Changling.
translations.idiomatic: At first, with government troops besieging Qingling and cutting off his line of retreat, Huaijin was afraid and consulted Yancheng magistrate Dong Changling.

sentences.zh: 昌齡母素誡其子令降，昌齡因此勸懷金歸款於光顏，且曰：「城中之人，父母妻子皆質於蔡州，如不屈而降，則家盡屠矣。

translations.literal: Changling's mother had always admonished her son to surrender; Changling therefore urged Huaijin to submit to Guangyan, saying: "The people in the city have parents, wives, and children all held hostage in Caizhou. If you do not pretend to resist before surrendering, their families will all be slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's mother had always admonished her son to surrender. Changling therefore urged Huaijin to submit to Guangyan, saying, "The people in the city have parents, wives, and children all held hostage in Caizhou. If you do not pretend to resist before surrendering, their families will all be slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 請來攻城，我則舉烽求救。

translations.literal: Ask them to come attack the city, and I will raise beacon fires to call for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Ask them to come attack the city, and I will raise beacon fires to call for rescue.

sentences.zh: 救兵將至，官軍逆擊之必敗，此時當以城降。」

translations.literal: When the relief force arrives, the government troops will surely be defeated if they strike against it; at that moment you should surrender the city."
translations.idiomatic: When the relief force arrives, the government troops will surely be defeated if they strike against it. At that moment you should surrender the city."

sentences.zh: 光顏從之，賊果敗走。

translations.literal: Guangyan followed this plan, and the rebels indeed fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan followed this plan, and the rebels indeed fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 於是昌齡執印，帥吏列於門外，懷金與諸將素服倒戈列於門內；

translations.literal: Thereupon Changling held the seal while the clerks and officers lined up outside the gate; Huaijin and the generals, in white dress with weapons reversed, lined up inside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Changling held the seal while the clerks and officers lined up outside the gate. Huaijin and the generals, dressed in white with weapons reversed, lined up inside the gate.

sentences.zh: 光顏受降，乃入羅城，其城自壞五十余步。

translations.literal: Guangyan accepted the surrender and then entered the outer city; fifty-odd paces of the wall collapsed of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted the surrender and then entered the outer city, where fifty-odd paces of the wall collapsed of themselves.

sentences.zh: 時韓弘為汴帥，驕矜倔強。

translations.literal: At the time Han Hong was military governor of Bian and was arrogant, proud, and obstinate.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Hong was military governor of Bian and was arrogant, proud, and obstinate.

sentences.zh: 常倚賊勢索朝廷姑息，惡光顏力戰，陰圖撓屈，計無所施。

translations.literal: He often relied on the rebels' strength to demand indulgence from the court, hated Guangyan's hard fighting, and secretly plotted to thwart him, but could find no means to do so.
translations.idiomatic: He often relied on the rebels' strength to demand indulgence from the court, hated Guangyan's hard fighting, and secretly plotted to thwart him, but could find no means to do so.

sentences.zh: 遂舉大梁城求得一美婦人，教以歌舞弦管六博之藝，飾之以珠翠金玉衣服之具，計費數百萬，命使者送遺光顏，冀一見悅惑而怠於軍政也。

translations.literal: He then searched the great city of Daliang until he found a beautiful woman, taught her the arts of song, dance, stringed music, and dice, adorned her with pearls, jade, gold, and fine garments at a cost of several million, and sent an envoy to present her to Guangyan, hoping that at one sight he would be delighted and distracted and slacken in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then searched the great city of Daliang until he found a beautiful woman, taught her song, dance, string music, and dice, adorned her with pearls, jade, gold, and fine garments at a cost of several million, and sent an envoy to present her to Guangyan, hoping that one sight of her would delight and distract him and make him slacken in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 使者即賫書先造光顏壘曰：「本使令公德公私愛，憂公暴露，欲進一妓，以慰公征役之思，謹以候命。」

translations.literal: The envoy first brought a letter to Guangyan's camp, saying: "Our commander, out of public and private regard for your virtue, is concerned that you endure exposure in the field and wishes to send a courtesan to comfort your thoughts on campaign. I await your command."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy first brought a letter to Guangyan's camp, saying, "Our commander, out of public and private regard for your virtue, is concerned that you endure exposure in the field and wishes to send a courtesan to comfort your thoughts on campaign. I await your command."

sentences.zh: 光顏曰：「今日已暮，明旦納焉。」

translations.literal: Guangyan said: "It is already evening today; I shall receive her tomorrow morning."
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan said, "It is already evening today. I shall receive her tomorrow morning."

sentences.zh: 詰朝，光顏乃大宴軍士；

translations.literal: At dawn Guangyan gave a great feast for his troops.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Guangyan gave a great feast for his troops.

sentences.zh: 三軍咸集，命使者進妓。

translations.literal: The whole army assembled, and he ordered the envoy to present the courtesan.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army assembled, and he ordered the envoy to present the courtesan.

sentences.zh: 妓至，則容止端麗，殆非人間所有，一座皆驚。

translations.literal: When the courtesan arrived, her bearing was graceful and lovely, as if scarcely of this world, and everyone at the feast was astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When the courtesan arrived, her bearing was graceful and lovely, as if scarcely of this world, and everyone at the feast was astonished.

sentences.zh: 光顏乃於座上謂來使曰：「令公憐光顏離家室久，舍美妓見贈，誠有以荷德也。

translations.literal: Guangyan then said to the envoy at the feast: "Your commander pities Guangyan for being long away from home and has sent this beautiful courtesan as a gift. I am truly grateful for such kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan then said to the envoy at the feast, "Your commander pities Guangyan for being long away from home and has sent this beautiful courtesan as a gift. I am truly grateful for such kindness.

sentences.zh: 然光顏受國家恩深，誓不與逆賊同生日月下。

translations.literal: Yet Guangyan has received deep favor from the state and swears not to live under the same sun and moon as the rebel traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guangyan has received deep favor from the state and swears not to live under the same sun and moon as the rebel traitors.

sentences.zh: 今戰卒數萬，皆背妻子，蹈白刃，光顏奈何以女色為樂？」

translations.literal: Now tens of thousands of fighting men have left wives and children behind and tread on naked blades—how can Guangyan take pleasure in women's beauty?"
translations.idiomatic: Now tens of thousands of fighting men have left wives and children behind and tread on naked blades. How can Guangyan take pleasure in women's beauty?"

sentences.zh: 言訖，涕泣嗚咽。

translations.literal: When he had finished speaking, he wept and sobbed.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished speaking, he wept and sobbed.

sentences.zh: 堂下兵士數萬，皆感激流涕。

translations.literal: The tens of thousands of soldiers below the hall were all moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: The tens of thousands of soldiers below the hall were all moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 乃厚以縑帛酬其來使，俾領其妓自席上而回，謂使者曰：「為光顏多謝令公。

translations.literal: He then richly rewarded the envoy with silk and had him lead the courtesan back from the feast, saying to the envoy: "Convey Guangyan's deep thanks to your commander.
translations.idiomatic: He then richly rewarded the envoy with silk and had him lead the courtesan back from the feast, saying to the envoy, "Convey Guangyan's deep thanks to your commander.

sentences.zh: 光顏事君許國之心，死無貳矣！」

translations.literal: Guangyan's heart in serving his ruler and pledging himself to the state will never waver unto death!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan's heart in serving his ruler and pledging himself to the state will never waver unto death!"

sentences.zh: 自此兵眾之心，彌加激勵。

translations.literal: From this the hearts of the troops were stirred all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From this the hearts of the troops were stirred all the more.

sentences.zh: 及裴度至行營，率賓從於方城沱口觀板築、五溝。

translations.literal: When Pei Du arrived at the field headquarters, he led his guests and attendants to Fangcheng Tuokou to inspect the stockade building and the Wugou works.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du arrived at the field headquarters, he led his guests and attendants to Fangcheng Tuokou to inspect the stockade building and the Wugou works.

sentences.zh: 賊遽至，註弩挺刃，勢將及度。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly arrived, strung their crossbows and brandished their blades, and were about to reach Du.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suddenly arrived, strung their crossbows and brandished their blades, and were about to reach Du.

sentences.zh: 光顏決戰於前以卻之。

translations.literal: Guangyan fought a decisive battle at the front to repel them.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan met them head-on in a pitched battle and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 時光顏預慮其來，先使田布以二百騎伏於溝中，出賊不意交擊之，度方獲免。

translations.literal: At that time Guangyan had anticipated their coming; he first sent Tian Bu with two hundred cavalry to lie in ambush in a ditch, and when they struck the enemy by surprise in a cross attack, Du was barely saved.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had foreseen the attack. He sent Tian Bu ahead with two hundred horsemen to hide in a ravine, then struck the rebels from an unexpected angle; Pei Du barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 布又先扼其溝中歸路，賊多棄騎越溝，相牽墜壓而死者千余人。

translations.literal: Bu also blocked their retreat route through the ditch in advance; many rebels abandoned their horses to cross the ditch, and more than a thousand died when they tripped, fell, and crushed one another.
translations.idiomatic: Bu had already cut off their escape through the ravine. Many rebels threw down their mounts and tried to scramble across; more than a thousand perished in the tangle, dragging one another down.

sentences.zh: 是日微光顏之救，度幾陷矣。

translations.literal: That day, but for Guangyan's rescue, Du would almost have been captured.
translations.idiomatic: Had Guangyan not come to the rescue that day, Pei Du would nearly have been lost.

sentences.zh: 是月，賊知光顏勇冠諸將，乃悉其眾出當光顏之師。

translations.literal: That month, the rebels learned that Guangyan's bravery surpassed that of all the other generals, and so they mustered their entire force to confront Guangyan's army.
translations.idiomatic: That month the rebels, knowing Guangyan outmatched every other commander in valor, threw their whole army against his line.

sentences.zh: 時李愬乘其無備，急引兵襲蔡州，拔之，獲元濟。

translations.literal: At that time Li Su, taking advantage of their lack of preparation, swiftly led his troops in a surprise attack on Cai Prefecture, captured it, and took Yuanji prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su seized the moment while they were unprepared, rushed his army against Cai Prefecture, took the city, and captured Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 董重質棄洄曲軍，入城降愬。

translations.literal: Dong Chongzhi abandoned the Huaiqu army, entered the city, and surrendered to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi deserted the Huaiqu garrison, entered the city, and submitted to Li Su.

sentences.zh: 光顏知之，躍馬入賊營，大呼以降，賊眾萬余人，皆解甲投戈請命。

translations.literal: When Guangyan learned of this, he leapt on his horse and rode into the rebel camp, shouting for them to surrender; more than ten thousand rebel troops all stripped off their armor, cast down their weapons, and pleaded for mercy.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan heard the news, spurred his horse straight into the rebel camp, and cried out for surrender. More than ten thousand men laid down arms and armor and begged for their lives.

sentences.zh: 賊平，加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was promoted to acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，命中官宴光顏於居第，賜芻米二十余車。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirteenth year, the emperor ordered eunuchs to host a banquet for Guangyan at his residence and bestowed upon him more than twenty cartloads of fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirteenth year, the court sent eunuchs to feast Guangyan at his home and granted him more than twenty wagonloads of fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 憲宗又禦麟德殿召對，賜金帶錦彩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong also received him in audience at the Linde Hall and granted him a gold belt and brocade silks.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong then summoned him to the Linde Hall, questioned him in person, and rewarded him with a gold belt and brocades.

sentences.zh: 朝廷東討李師道，授光顏義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the court launched an eastern campaign against Li Shidao, Guangyan was appointed military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: As the court marched east against Li Shidao, Guangyan was made military governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，尋赴行營。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, he soon proceeded to the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He had scarcely arrived at his command when he went on to join the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數旬之內，再敗賊軍於濮陽，殺戮數千人，進軍深入。

translations.literal: Within several dozen days, he twice defeated the rebel army at Puyang, slaughtering several thousand men, and advanced deep into enemy territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the space of a few weeks he twice routed the rebels at Puyang, killing several thousand, and pressed deep into their territory.

sentences.zh: 十四年，西蕃入寇，移授邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, when the Western Tibetans invaded, he was reassigned as military governor of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, with the Tibetans raiding from the west, he was transferred to command Binning.

sentences.zh: 時鹽州為吐蕃所毀，命李文悅為刺史，令光顏充勾當修築鹽州城使。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Prefecture had been destroyed by the Tibetans; Li Wenyue was appointed prefect, and Guangyan was ordered to serve as commissioner in charge of rebuilding the walls of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Prefecture lay in ruins after Tibetan attacks. Li Wenyue was named prefect, and Guangyan was put in charge of rebuilding the city's walls.

sentences.zh: 仍許以陳許六千人隨赴邠寧。

translations.literal: He was also permitted to bring six thousand men from Chen and Xu to accompany him to Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He was allowed to take six thousand troops from Chen and Xu with him to Binning.

sentences.zh: 是歲，吐蕃侵涇原。

translations.literal: That year, the Tibetans invaded Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the Tibetans struck Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 自田縉鎮夏州，以貪猥侵撓党項羌，乃引吐蕃入寇。

translations.literal: Ever since Tian Ji had been stationed at Xia Prefecture, his greed and misconduct in harassing the Tangut Qiang had drawn the Tibetans into raiding.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Tian Ji governed Xia Prefecture, his greed and bullying of the Tangut Qiang had provoked Tibetan incursions.

sentences.zh: 及蕃軍攻涇州，邊將郝玼血戰始退。

translations.literal: When the Tibetan army attacked Jing Prefecture, the border general Hao Ci fought a bloody battle before they finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans besieged Jing Prefecture, the frontier commander Hao Ci bled them in fierce fighting before they retreated.

sentences.zh: 初，光顏聞賊攻涇州，料兵赴救，邠師喧然曰：「人給五十千而不識戰陣，彼何人也！

translations.literal: At first, when Guangyan heard the rebels were attacking Jing Prefecture, he gathered troops to go to the rescue; the soldiers of Bin were in an uproar, saying, "They pay us fifty thousand cash each, yet we don't even know battle formations — who are those people!
translations.idiomatic: When Guangyan heard the enemy was pressing Jing Prefecture, he mustered his men to march to its relief. The Binning troops erupted in protest: "They give those men fifty thousand cash apiece, and they can't even hold a battle line — who are they, anyway?

sentences.zh: 常額衣資不得而前蹈白刃，此何人也！」

translations.literal: We can't even get our regular pay and clothing allowance, yet we're sent forward to face naked blades — what sort of people are they!"
translations.idiomatic: We never see our regular wages or kit, yet we're the ones marched out to walk into naked steel — what kind of men are we supposed to be!"

sentences.zh: 憤聲恟々不可遏。

translations.literal: Their angry voices rose in a tumult that could not be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: Their fury swelled into a clamor no one could quiet.

sentences.zh: 光顏素得士心，曲為陳說大義，言發涕流。

translations.literal: Guangyan had always won the hearts of his soldiers; he earnestly set forth the greater cause, and as he spoke, tears streamed down his face.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had long held the army's loyalty. He pleaded the larger cause with such feeling that tears ran down his face as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 三軍感之，亦泣下，乃欣然即路，擊賊退之。

translations.literal: The whole army was moved and wept as well; then they gladly set out on the march, attacked the rebels, and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: The entire host was moved to tears. They then took the road willingly, struck the enemy, and beat them back.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，就加特進，仍與一子四品正員官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Guangyan was immediately promoted to Grand Censor, and one of his sons was granted a regular fourth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: On Muzong's accession, Guangyan was at once raised to grand censor, and one of his sons received a regular fourth-rank post.

sentences.zh: 尋詔赴闕，賜開化裏第，進加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to court, granted a residence on Kaihua Lane, and further promoted to co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon called to the capital, given a mansion on Kaihua Lane, and elevated to co-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 穆宗以光顏功冠諸將，故召赴闕，宴賜優給。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, because Guangyan's achievements surpassed those of all other generals, summoned him to court and entertained him with generous gifts and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, holding Guangyan's deeds above every other general's, summoned him to court and lavished feasts and gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 已而帶平章復鎮，所以報勛臣也。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, he returned to his command while retaining his title of chief minister — a way of repaying a meritorious subject.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went back to the frontier still bearing the title of chief minister — the court's way of honoring a man who had earned it.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，遷鳳翔節度使，依前檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing he was transferred to military commissioner of Fengxiang, retaining his former ranks as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Changqing era he became military commissioner of Fengxiang, keeping his titles as acting Minister of Works and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 歲末，復授許州節度使。

translations.literal: At year's end he was again appointed military commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year was out he was reassigned as military commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以光顏昔鎮陳許，頗得士心，將討鎮、冀，故有此拜。

translations.literal: Because Guangyan had once governed Chen and Xu and had well won the troops' hearts, and because the court intended to campaign against Zhen and Ji, this appointment was made.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan had once held Chen-Xu and won deep loyalty from the ranks. With a campaign against Zhen and Ji in view, the court gave him this post.

sentences.zh: 赴鎮日，宰相百僚以故事送別於章敬寺，穆宗禦通化門臨送之，賜錦彩、銀器、良馬、玉帶等物。

translations.literal: On the day he departed for his post, chancellors and the hundred officials saw him off according to custom at Zhangjing Temple; Muzong proceeded to Tonghua Gate to send him off in person and bestowed brocade silks, silver vessels, fine horses, a jade belt, and other gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left for his command, the full court saw him off at Zhangjing Temple by custom. Muzong went in person to Tonghua Gate to farewell him, gifting brocades, silverware, fine horses, and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 二年，討王廷湊，命光顏兼深州行營諸軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year, campaigning against Wang Tingcou, Guangyan was ordered to serve concurrently as military commissioner of all armies in the Shenzhou forward camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, for the campaign against Wang Tingcou, he was named overall commander of the Shenzhou expedition.

sentences.zh: 光顏既受命而行，懸軍討賊，艱於饋運。

translations.literal: Once Guangyan accepted the commission and set out, his army advanced deep into hostile country to attack rebels, and supply transport proved arduous.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan accepted the command and marched out, but his army was deep in enemy territory and supply lines quickly became a struggle.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又以滄、景、德、棣等州俾之兼管，以其鄰賊之郡，可便飛挽。

translations.literal: The court also put Cang, Jing, De, Di, and other prefectures under his concurrent administration, since those districts bordered the rebels and could speed emergency transport.
translations.idiomatic: The court added Cang, Jing, De, Di, and neighboring prefectures to his jurisdiction, hoping their proximity to the enemy would ease rapid resupply.

sentences.zh: 光顏以朝廷制置乖方，賊帥連結，未可朝夕平定，事若差跌，即前功悉棄，乃懇辭兼鎮。

translations.literal: Guangyan held that the court's dispositions were ill judged—the rebel chieftains were linked together and could not be settled overnight; if affairs stumbled, all prior merit would be squandered—and he earnestly declined the additional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan argued the court's plan was unsound: the rebel leaders were allied and would not fall quickly, and one misstep would waste everything already won. He begged off the extra territories.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾作，表祈歸鎮。

translations.literal: Soon illness set in and he memorialized asking to return to his original command.
translations.idiomatic: He soon fell ill and petitioned to return to his own headquarters.

sentences.zh: 朝廷果討賊無功而赦廷湊。

translations.literal: The court indeed failed to subdue the rebels and pardoned Tingcou.
translations.idiomatic: As he had foreseen, the campaign failed and the court pardoned Wang Tingcou.

sentences.zh: 四年，敬宗即位，正拜司徒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jingzong succeeded to the throne, and Guangyan was formally appointed Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Jingzong took the throne and Guangyan was formally made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 汴州李絺逐其帥叛，詔光顏率陳許之師討之。

translations.literal: When Li Xi of Bian Prefecture drove out his commander and rebelled, Guangyan was ordered to lead the Chen-Xu army to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi of Bianzhou expelled his commander and rose in revolt, Guangyan was commanded to lead the Chen-Xu forces against him.

sentences.zh: 營於尉氏，俄而誅絺。

translations.literal: He encamped at Weishi, and before long Li Xi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He pitched camp at Weishi, and within a short time Li Xi was put to death.

sentences.zh: 遷太原尹、北京留守、河東節度使，進階開府儀同三司，仍於正衙受冊司徒兼侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Governor of Taiyuan, Garrison Commander of the Northern Capital, and military governor of Hedong; promoted to Senior General of the Palace with Honorary Three Excellencies; and at the main court received investiture as Grand Preceptor and concurrently Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Taiyuan, garrison commander of the Northern Capital, and military governor of Hedong; advanced to senior general of the palace with honorary three excellencies; and in the main hall received formal investiture as grand preceptor and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 二年九月卒，年六十六，廢朝三日，贈太尉，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year he died at the age of sixty-six; court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and given the posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of the second year, aged sixty-six. Court mourning lasted three days. He was posthumously made grand commandant and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 烏重胤，潞州牙將也。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin was a garrison officer of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin served as a garrison officer in Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和中，王承宗叛，王師加討。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, Wang Chengzong rebelled and imperial troops were dispatched to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe reign, Wang Chengzong rose in rebellion, and the imperial armies marched to crush him.

sentences.zh: 潞帥盧從史雖出軍，而密與賊通。

translations.literal: The military governor of Lu, Lu Congshi, though he sent out troops, secretly colluded with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi, the Lu commander, marched his men out in name but secretly trafficked with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時神策行營吐突承璀與從史軍相近，承璀與重胤謀，縛從史於帳下。

translations.literal: At that time Tuhutu Chengchan of the Shence Field Army was camped near Lu Congshi's forces; Chengchan conspired with Chongyin and bound Congshi in his tent.
translations.idiomatic: Tuhutu Chengchan of the Shence Field Army was then encamped near Congshi's force. Chengchan plotted with Chongyin and seized Congshi in his own tent.

sentences.zh: 是日，重胤戒嚴，潞軍無敢動者。

translations.literal: That day Chongyin declared martial law, and none of the Lu troops dared stir.
translations.idiomatic: That day Chongyin put the camp under strict guard, and not a man in the Lu army dared move.

sentences.zh: 憲宗賞其功，授潞府左司馬，遷懷州刺史，兼充河陽三城節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong rewarded his service, appointing him Left Deputy Military Commissioner of Lu Prefecture, then transferring him to be Prefect of Huaizhou and concurrently military governor of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong rewarded the deed by making him left deputy military commissioner of Lu, then prefect of Huaizhou and military governor of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 會討淮、蔡，用重胤壓境，仍割汝州隸河陽。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Huai and Cai began, Chongyin was used to press the border, and Runan Prefecture was detached and placed under Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai-Cai campaign opened, Chongyin was deployed to pin the enemy along the frontier, and Runan Prefecture was transferred to Heyang's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 自王師討淮西三年，重胤與李光顏掎角相應，大小百余戰，以至元濟誅。

translations.literal: From the three years of the imperial campaign against Huai-West, Chongyin and Li Guangyan coordinated their forces in pincer fashion, fighting more than a hundred battles large and small, until Yuanji was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Through the three-year war against Huai-West, Chongyin and Li Guangyan worked in concert, fighting more than a hundred engagements, large and small, until Yuanji was brought to justice.

sentences.zh: 就加檢校尚書右僕射，轉司空。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Acting Vice Director of the Right Department of the Secretariat and transferred to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly made acting vice director of the right Secretariat and then grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 蔡將有李端者，過溵河降重胤。

translations.literal: Among the Cai generals was one named Li Duan, who crossed the Wen River and surrendered to Chongyin.
translations.idiomatic: One of the Cai commanders, Li Duan, crossed the Wen River and defected to Chongyin.

sentences.zh: 其妻為賊束縛於樹，臠食至死，將絕，猶呼其夫曰：「善事烏僕射。」

translations.literal: His wife was bound to a tree by the rebels, who carved flesh from her and fed on it until she died; as her life ebbed away, she still called out to her husband, "Serve Vice Director Wu well."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels tied his wife to a tree and cut flesh from her living body until she died. Even at the end she called to her husband: "Serve Vice Director Wu faithfully."

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which he had won people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: That was how deeply he had won men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，代鄭權為橫海軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe, he replaced Zheng Quan as military governor of the Henghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he succeeded Zheng Quan as military governor of the Henghai Army.

sentences.zh: 既至鎮，上言曰：「臣以河朔能拒朝命者，其大略可見。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his post, he submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject believes the general pattern by which Hebei can defy the court's commands is already clear.
translations.idiomatic: On taking command he memorialized the throne: "Your servant believes the reason Hebei has been able to defy the court is already plain to see.

sentences.zh: 蓋刺史失其職，反使鎮將領兵事。

translations.literal: It is essentially that the prefects have lost their proper duties, while the garrison generals instead take charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects have been stripped of their proper duties, while garrison commanders have seized military authority instead.

sentences.zh: 若刺史各得職分，又有鎮兵，則節將雖有祿山、思明之奸，豈能據一州為叛哉？

translations.literal: If each prefect could properly perform his office and the garrison troops remained under imperial control, then even if a military commissioner possessed the treachery of An Lushan or Shi Siming, how could he seize a single prefecture and rebel?
translations.idiomatic: If every prefect held his rightful office and garrison troops answered to the throne, then even a commissioner with the cunning of An Lushan or Shi Siming could not hold one prefecture and rebel.

sentences.zh: 所以河朔六十年能拒朝命者，只以奪刺史、縣令之職，自作威福故也。

translations.literal: The reason Hebei has been able to resist the court's orders for sixty years is simply that prefects and county magistrates have been stripped of their offices, allowing the military governors to wield power and bestow favors as they please.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei has defied the court for sixty years only because prefects and magistrates were dispossessed of their posts, leaving the military governors to rule by whim.

sentences.zh: 臣所管德、棣、景三州，已舉公牒，各還刺史職事訖，應在州兵，並令刺史收管。

translations.literal: In the three prefectures of De, Di, and Jing under my jurisdiction, I have issued official documents restoring each prefect to his proper duties; all troops stationed in those prefectures have been placed under the prefects' command.
translations.idiomatic: In De, Di, and Jing, the three prefectures under my command, I have already issued orders restoring each prefect to his duties and putting all local troops under prefectural control.

sentences.zh: 又景州本是弓高縣，請卻廢為縣，歸化縣本是草市，請廢縣依舊屬德州。」

translations.literal: Furthermore, Jing Prefecture was originally Gonggao County — I request that it be abolished and restored to county status; Guihua County was originally a rural market — I request that the county be abolished and it be returned to De Prefecture as before."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Prefecture was once Gonggao County — I ask that it be abolished and made a county again. Guihua County began as a country market — I ask that it be abolished and returned to De Prefecture as before."

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: The edict approved all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved every request.

sentences.zh: 由是法制修立，各歸名分。

translations.literal: Thereafter the laws and regulations were properly established, and each office returned to its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the laws were set in order and every office resumed its proper name and rank.

sentences.zh: 及屯軍深州，重胤以朝廷制置失宜，賊方憑淩，未可輕進，觀望累月。

translations.literal: When he stationed his army at Shen Prefecture, Chongyin judged that the court's dispositions were ill-advised and that the rebels were still ascendant, so that it was inadvisable to advance rashly; he held back and watched for many months.
translations.idiomatic: When he encamped at Shen Prefecture, Chongyin concluded that the court's strategy was unsound and the rebels still held the upper hand, so a reckless advance would be folly. He held his position and waited for months.

sentences.zh: 穆宗急於誅叛，遂以杜叔良代之，以重胤檢校司徒，兼興元尹，充山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong, eager to suppress the rebellion quickly, replaced him with Du Shuliang; Chongyin was appointed honorary Grand Preceptor, concurrently Governor of Xingyuan, and military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong, impatient to finish the rebellion, replaced him with Du Shuliang and made Chongyin honorary grand preceptor, governor of Xingyuan, and military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，復以本官為天平軍節度、鄆曹濮等州觀察等使。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, he was again appointed with his existing rank as military governor of Tianping and oversight commissioner for Yan, Cao, Pu, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Called to the capital, he was once more given his former rank as military governor of Tianping and oversight commissioner over Yan, Cao, Pu, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 李同捷據滄州，請襲父位，朝廷不從。

translations.literal: Li Tongjie held Cang Prefecture and petitioned to succeed his father's position; the court refused.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tongjie occupied Cang Prefecture and asked to inherit his father's command; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 議者慮狡童拒命，欲以重臣代。

translations.literal: Counsellors feared the cunning youth would defy orders and wished to send a senior minister in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers worried the young rebel would resist and urged that a senior commander replace the current general.

sentences.zh: 乃移鎮兗海，加太子太師、平章事，俾兼領滄景節度，仍舊割齊州隸之，蓋望不勞師而底定。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to govern Yan-Hai, promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince and chief minister, and charged to concurrently govern Cang-Jing Circuit; Qi Prefecture was again detached and attached to his command — all in the hope of settling matters without raising troops.
translations.idiomatic: So he was shifted to Yan-Hai, made grand preceptor of the crown prince and chief minister, and told to take over Cang-Jing as well, with Qi Prefecture again placed under his command — the court hoping to settle the affair without another campaign.

sentences.zh: 制出旬日，重胤卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Within ten days after the edict was issued, Chongyin died; he was posthumously appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Ten days after the appointment was promulgated, Chongyin died. He was posthumously made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 重胤出自行間，及為長帥，赤心奉上。

translations.literal: Chongyin had risen from the ranks; once he became a senior commander, he served the throne with undivided loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin came up through the ranks, and once he held high command he served the throne with an open heart.

sentences.zh: 能與下同甘苦，所至立功，未嘗矜伐。

translations.literal: He shared hardship and comfort with his subordinates, achieved merit wherever he was posted, and never boasted of his accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: He shared the soldiers' hardships and comforts, won victories wherever he was sent, and never vaunted his deeds.

sentences.zh: 而善待賓寮，禮分同至，當時名士，鹹願依之。

translations.literal: He also treated his staff with kindness and courtesy to the highest degree; eminent men of the day all wished to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated his officers and guests with exceptional courtesy, and leading men of the age were eager to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 身歿之日，軍士二十余人，皆割股肉以為祭酹，雖古之名將，無以加焉。

translations.literal: On the day of his death, more than twenty soldiers cut flesh from their thighs as sacrificial offerings to him — even the famed generals of antiquity could not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, more than twenty soldiers cut flesh from their own thighs as offerings to his spirit — a devotion that not even the great generals of old could exceed.

sentences.zh: 子漢弘嗣，起復授左領軍衛將軍。

translations.literal: His son Han Hongsi was granted leave from mourning to accept appointment as General of the Left Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han Hongsi was recalled from mourning and appointed general of the left imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 漢弘上表乞終服紀，文宗嘉詔從之。

translations.literal: Han Hong submitted a memorial requesting to complete his mourning period; Emperor Wenzong commended him and granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong petitioned to finish his full term of mourning. Wenzong praised his filial intent and granted it.

sentences.zh: 服闋，方授官。

translations.literal: Only after his mourning was complete was he formally given the office.
translations.idiomatic: Not until his mourning ended was the appointment formally conferred.

sentences.zh: 王沛，許州人。

translations.literal: Wang Pei was a native of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei came from Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 年十八，有勇決。

translations.literal: At the age of eighteen, he was brave and resolute.
translations.idiomatic: By eighteen he was already bold and decisive.

sentences.zh: 許州節度使上官涚奇其才，以女妻之，署為牙門將。

translations.literal: The military governor of Xu, Shangguan Shui, admired his talent, gave him his daughter in marriage, and appointed him as a garrison officer.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Shui, military governor of Xu, took notice of his ability, gave him his daughter in marriage, and made him a garrison officer.

sentences.zh: 及涚卒，子婿田偁迫脅涚子，欲邀襲位，懼監軍使不順其事，將結謀伏兵以圖之。

translations.literal: When Shui died, his son-in-law Tian Cheng coerced Shui's son, intending to seize the commander's post; fearing the army supervisor would not go along with the plot, he planned to set an ambush.
translations.idiomatic: After Shui's death, his son-in-law Tian Cheng intimidated Shui's son and tried to seize the command for himself. Fearing the army supervisor would block the scheme, he plotted to lay an ambush.

sentences.zh: 沛竊知其謀，密告監軍，因盡擒其黨於伏匿之所。

translations.literal: Pei secretly learned of the scheme, informed the army supervisor, and had all the conspirators seized at their hiding place.
translations.idiomatic: Pei learned of the plot in secret, warned the army supervisor, and had the whole faction seized at their hiding place.

sentences.zh: 監軍範日用以其事聞，德宗乃以陳許行軍司馬劉昌裔總統其軍，賜沛手詔，令護涚之子赴上都。

translations.literal: The army supervisor Fan Riyong reported the matter; Emperor Dezong sent Liu Changyi, campaigning marshal of Chen-Xu, to take overall command of the army, and issued Pei an imperial missive ordering him to escort Shui's son to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Fan Riyong reported the affair. Dezong put Liu Changyi, campaigning marshal of Chen-Xu, in overall command and sent Pei an imperial letter ordering him to escort Shui's son to the capital.

sentences.zh: 既至，召見，德宗謂之曰：「據卿忠義，寵宜加等。

translations.literal: When Pei arrived and was received in audience, Dezong said to him, "Given your loyalty and righteousness, your honors should be elevated by a full rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei arrived and was summoned before the throne, Dezong told him, "For loyalty such as yours, reward should rise by more than one step.

sentences.zh: 但昌裔所奏，只請加監察御史，朕意殊為不足。

translations.literal: But in Changyi's memorial, he only requested appointment as Supervising Censor — in my view that is far from adequate.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Changyi's memorial asks only for supervising censor — far too little in my judgment.

sentences.zh: 卿速歸，便宣付昌裔，更令奏來。」

translations.literal: Return at once, relay this order to Changyi, and have him submit a new memorial."
translations.idiomatic: Go back at once, deliver my word to Changyi, and have him submit a new recommendation."

sentences.zh: 遂驛騎而還。

translations.literal: And so Pei rode post-horses back.
translations.idiomatic: Pei then galloped home by relay horse.

sentences.zh: 未至許州，拜開府儀同三司、兼御史中丞，依前本職。

translations.literal: Before he reached Xu Prefecture, he was appointed Senior General of the Palace with Honorary Three Excellencies and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, while retaining his original position.
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached Xu Prefecture, he was named senior general of the palace with honorary three excellencies and vice censor-in-chief, while keeping his former post.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟反，李光顏受命攻討，奇沛節概，署行營兵馬使，別統勁兵屯於近郊。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Li Guangyan was ordered to attack and suppress him; impressed by Pei's fortitude and integrity, he appointed him field army commander and assigned him a separate force of crack troops encamped near the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji rebelled, Li Guangyan was sent to suppress him. Struck by Pei's strength of character, he made him field army commander and gave him a picked force encamped outside the city.

sentences.zh: 及軍合，連破蔡寇。

translations.literal: When the armies united, they repeatedly routed the Cai rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies joined, they broke the Cai forces again and again.

sentences.zh: 頻詔進軍，諸將觀望，無敢先渡溵河。

translations.literal: The court repeatedly ordered an advance, but the generals held back; none dared cross the Wen River first.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial orders to advance came again and again, yet the generals hung back — none would be first to cross the Wen River.

sentences.zh: 沛率兵五千，夜渡溵河合流口，徑扼賊喉而成城。

translations.literal: Pei led five thousand men, crossed the Wen River at its confluence by night, and seized the rebel throat-hold to establish a fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Pei took five thousand men, forded the Wen at its confluence by night, and seized the enemy's vital crossing, building a fortified camp there.

sentences.zh: 自是，河陽、宣武、太原、魏博等軍繼渡，掎角進攻郾城。

translations.literal: Thereafter the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Taiyuan, Weibo, and others crossed in succession and advanced in pincer fashion against Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After that the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Taiyuan, Weibo, and others crossed in turn and closed on Yancheng from several sides.

sentences.zh: 沛先結壘與賊對，賊將鄧懷金率眾面縛而降。

translations.literal: Pei first built fortifications facing the enemy camp; the rebel general Deng Huaijin led his men forward with bound hands to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Pei first raised fortifications opposite the enemy lines. The rebel commander Deng Huaijin came forward with his hands bound and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊平。

translations.literal: The Cai rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Cai rebellion was crushed.

sentences.zh: 沛隨李光顏入朝，光顏具陳沛功，加御史大夫。

translations.literal: Pei accompanied Li Guangyan to court; Guangyan fully recounted Pei's merits, and Pei was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Pei went to court with Li Guangyan, who laid out his achievements in full. Pei was promoted to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 既還鎮，光顏受詔討鄆寇。

translations.literal: After returning to his post, Guangyan received orders to campaign against the rebels of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the field, Guangyan was ordered to campaign against the Yan rebels.

sentences.zh: 及李師道誅，詔分許州兵戍於邠，以沛為都將，救鹽州，擊退吐蕃。

translations.literal: After Li Shidao was executed, an edict detached troops from Xu Prefecture to garrison Bin; Pei was made chief commander, rescued Yan Prefecture, and repelled the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao's execution, part of the Xu garrison was sent to Bin. Pei served as chief commander, relieved Yan Prefecture, and drove back the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 以功加寧州刺史，遷陳州。

translations.literal: For this achievement he was promoted to Prefect of Ningzhou and transferred to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made prefect of Ningzhou and transferred to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李絺反，詔沛兼忠武節度副使，率師討絺。

translations.literal: When Li Xi rebelled, Pei was ordered to serve concurrently as deputy military governor of Zhongwu and lead troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi rebelled, Pei was named deputy military governor of Zhongwu and sent to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 絺平，加檢校右散騎常侍，遷兗海沂密節度、觀察等使。

translations.literal: When Li Xi was pacified, Pei was promoted to honorary Right Regular Mounted Attendant and transferred to be military governor and oversight commissioner of Yan-Hai, Yi, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xi was put down, Pei was made honorary right regular mounted attendant and military governor and oversight commissioner of Yan-Hai, Yi, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 此邦新造，人情獷驁，沛明申法令，選蒐軍政，期年大理。

translations.literal: This region had only recently been established; the people were fierce and unruly. Pei clearly proclaimed the laws, carefully inspected military and civil administration, and within a year brought great order.
translations.idiomatic: The territory was newly pacified and the people rough and hard to govern. Pei made the laws plain, tightened military and civil discipline, and within a year the region was well ordered.

sentences.zh: 明年，改檢校工部尚書，充忠武軍節度、陳許蔡觀察等使。

translations.literal: The next year he was reassigned as honorary Minister of Works and appointed military governor of Zhongwu and oversight commissioner of Chen, Xu, and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became honorary minister of works, military governor of Zhongwu, and oversight commissioner over Chen, Xu, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 卒於鎮，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: He died in his post and was posthumously appointed Vice Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: He died in command and was posthumously made vice director of the right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子逢。

translations.literal: His son was Wang Feng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wang Feng.

sentences.zh: 逢，少沈勇，從父征伐有功，為忠武都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: Feng was calm and brave from youth; he followed his father on campaigns and rendered distinguished service, serving as chief military commander of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was steady and courageous from boyhood. He campaigned with his father to good effect and became chief controller of military affairs for Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 太和中，入宿衛，歷諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: During the Taihe era he entered palace guard service and held successive posts as general of various guard units.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe reign he entered the palace guard and rose through commands in several guard regiments.

sentences.zh: 從石雄、劉沔破回紇於天德。

translations.literal: He joined Shi Xiong and Liu Mian in defeating the Uyghurs at Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: He fought under Shi Xiong and Liu Mian to defeat the Uyghurs at Tiande.

sentences.zh: 性果決，用法嚴。

translations.literal: He was resolute by nature and strict in enforcing the law.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was decisive, and he enforced the law without leniency.

sentences.zh: 其時有二千人不上陣，官賜賞給，逢皆不與。

translations.literal: At that time there were two thousand men who did not take the field; when officials distributed reward stipends, Feng gave none of them any.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, two thousand soldiers had not gone into battle. When the authorities handed out rewards, Feng refused to give any of them a share.

sentences.zh: 或非之，逢曰：「健兒向前冒白刃，若無功而賞，其如冒刃者何？」

translations.literal: Some criticized this. Feng said: "Brave soldiers go forward and face naked blades—if those without merit are rewarded, what shall become of those who faced the blades?"
translations.idiomatic: Some objected, but Feng said: "My men marched forward into naked steel. If I reward men who did nothing, what honor is left for those who truly risked their lives?"

sentences.zh: 王宰攻劉稹，逢領陳許七千人屯翼城，代田令昭。

translations.literal: When Wang Zai attacked Liu Cong, Feng led seven thousand Chen-Xu troops to garrison Yicheng, replacing Tian Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zai marched against Liu Cong, Feng took seven thousand Chen-Xu troops to hold Yicheng, relieving Tian Lingzhao.

sentences.zh: 賊平，檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, he was made Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 累遷至忠武軍節度、陳許觀察等使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted until he became Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Observation Commissioner of Chen-Xu, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments until he held the posts of Military Commissioner of the Zhongwu Army and Observation Commissioner of Chen-Xu.

sentences.zh: 李珙，山東甲姓，代修婚姻。

translations.literal: Li Gong came from a leading clan of Shandong; for generations the family had maintained marriage alliances.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gong belonged to one of Shandong's great clans, a house that for generations had cemented its standing through marriage alliances.

sentences.zh: 至珙，不好讀書，唯以弓馬為務。

translations.literal: When it came to Gong, he did not like reading books and devoted himself only to bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Gong himself cared little for books and gave himself over entirely to archery and horsemanship.

sentences.zh: 長六尺余，氣貌魁岸。

translations.literal: He was more than six chi in height, and in bearing and appearance he was towering and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than six chi tall, with a frame and presence that seemed carved from granite.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣澤潞謁李抱真，異之，將選為衙門將，旋以酒酣使氣，復欲棄之。

translations.literal: Once he went to Ze-Lu to pay his respects to Li Baozhen, who was struck by him and was about to select him as a gate guard general; but then, because he grew overbearing when drunk, Baozhen again wished to cast him aside.
translations.idiomatic: Once he visited Li Baozhen in Ze-Lu. Baozhen was impressed and was on the point of making him a gate guard general, but Gong grew arrogant in his cups, and Baozhen nearly turned his back on him.

sentences.zh: 都將王虔休謂抱真曰：「李珙，奇士也，若不能用，不如殺之，無為他人所得。」

translations.literal: The commander Wang Qianxiu said to Baozhen: 'Li Gong is an extraordinary man. If you cannot use him, you had better kill him—do not let another obtain him.'
translations.idiomatic: The commander Wang Qianxiu told Baozhen, 'Li Gong is no ordinary man. If you will not employ him, kill him—do not let some rival win him over.'

sentences.zh: 抱真死，虔休為帥，乃依虔休，累為昭義大將。

translations.literal: When Baozhen died and Qianxiu became commander, Gong then attached himself to Qianxiu and rose repeatedly until he became a major general of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: After Baozhen's death, when Qianxiu took command, Gong entered his service and rose step by step to become a senior general of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 吐突承璀之擒盧從史，烏重胤實預其謀，珙初不知，將救從史。

translations.literal: In Tutu Chengcui's capture of Lu Congshi, Wu Chongyin had actually taken part in the plot; Gong at first did not know this and was about to go rescue Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Tutu Chengcui seized Lu Congshi, Wu Chongyin had secretly helped plan the affair. Gong knew nothing of this at first and was preparing to ride to Congshi's rescue.

sentences.zh: 聞重胤受朝旨，乃觀望不進，重胤以此德之。

translations.literal: When he heard that Chongyin had received the court's orders, he then held back and did not advance; Chongyin on this account was grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Chongyin had received the court's commission, he halted and did not move forward, and Chongyin counted this as a debt of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 後領河陽，乃置於麾下。

translations.literal: Later, when [Chongyin] took command of Heyang, he placed [Gong] under his own command.
translations.idiomatic: Later, once Chongyin assumed command of Heyang, he brought Gong under his banner.

sentences.zh: 然朝廷以與從史厚善，竟出為北邊一校。

translations.literal: Yet because the court knew he had been on close terms with Congshi, in the end he was sent out as a petty officer on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The court, however, remembered his close friendship with Congshi and in the end relegated him to a lowly post on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 元和十年，征淮西，重胤懇表為諸道行營都虞候，詔特從之，俄以母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, during the campaign against Huaixi, Chongyin earnestly memorialized to have him appointed overall adjutant of the circuit expeditionary camps; the edict specially granted this, but soon afterward he left office due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yuanhe, when the empire marched on Huaixi, Chongyin pleaded earnestly to have him made overall adjutant of the expeditionary camps. The throne granted the request, but before long Gong resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除右武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he was appointed Senior General of the Right Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning was complete, he was appointed Senior General of the Right Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年八月卒，年六十四，廢朝一日。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year of Changqing he died at the age of sixty-four; court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the fourth year of Changqing, at sixty-four. The court suspended audiences for a day.

sentences.zh: 李祐，本蔡州牙將。

translations.literal: Li You was originally a garrison officer of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li You had begun as a garrison officer in Cai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事吳元濟，驍勇善戰。

translations.literal: He served Wu Yuanji, and was fierce, brave, and skilled in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He served Wu Yuanji—a man fierce in spirit, bold in action, and formidable on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 自王師討淮西，祐為行營將，每抗官軍，皆憚之。

translations.literal: From the time the imperial army campaigned against Huaixi, You served as an expeditionary camp general; whenever he resisted the government army, all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial armies marched against Huaixi, You became an expeditionary general, and every time he stood in their path the government troops feared him.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，為李愬所擒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, he was captured by Li Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Li Su took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 愬知祐有膽略，釋其死，厚遇之。

translations.literal: Su knew You had courage and stratagem, released him from death, and treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Su saw that You possessed both courage and cunning, spared his life, and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 推誠定分，與同寢食，往往帳中密語，達曙不寐。

translations.literal: He extended full sincerity and fixed his role, sharing sleeping quarters and meals with him; often they spoke in secret in the tent until dawn without sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: Su opened his heart to him, fixed his place at his side, and shared bed and board with him. Often they talked alone in the tent until dawn, neither man sleeping.

sentences.zh: 人有耳屬於外者，但屢聞祐感泣聲。

translations.literal: Those who had ears attuned to the outside only repeatedly heard the sound of You weeping in emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Men listening outside the tent heard again and again the sound of You weeping.

sentences.zh: 而軍中以前時為祐殺傷者多，營壘諸卒會議，皆恨不殺祐。

translations.literal: But in the army, because many had been killed or wounded by You in earlier fighting, the soldiers in the camps met in council and all hated that You had not been killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet many in the army had fallen to You's hand in earlier battles, and when the men gathered in camp they cursed Su for not having killed him.

sentences.zh: 愬以眾情歸怨，慮不能全，因送祐於京師，乃上表救之。
