translations.literal: Su, because popular sentiment turned to resentment, feared he could not keep You safe, and so sent You to the capital while submitting a memorial pleading for his life.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the army's anger turn against You, Su feared he could not protect him and sent him to the capital while memorializing the throne to spare his life.

sentences.zh: 憲宗特恕，遂遣祐賜愬。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong specially pardoned him and then sent You back as a gift to Su.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong granted a special pardon and returned You to Su as a gift from the throne.

sentences.zh: 愬大喜，即以三千精兵付之。

translations.literal: Su was greatly delighted and immediately entrusted three thousand elite troops to him.
translations.idiomatic: Su was overjoyed and at once placed three thousand picked troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 祐聽言，無有所疑，竟以祐破蔡，擒元濟。

translations.literal: Su listened to his words without any doubt, and in the end relied on You to break Cai and capture Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: Su believed every word he said without hesitation, and in the end it was You who broke Cai and seized Yuanji.

sentences.zh: 以功授神武將軍，遷金吾將軍、檢校左散騎常侍、夏州刺史、御史大夫、夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Divine Martial Guard, then promoted to General of the Golden Guard, Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Prefect of Xia Prefecture, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was made General of the Divine Martial Guard, then promoted through the ranks to General of the Golden Guard, Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Prefect of Xia, Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，入為右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoli reign he entered [the capital] as Senior General of the Right Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Baoli reign he was recalled to serve as Senior General of the Right Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋以吐蕃入寇，出為涇州刺史、涇原節度使。

translations.literal: Soon, because Tibet invaded, he was sent out as Prefect of Jing Prefecture and Military Commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet raided the borders, he was sent out as Prefect of Jing and Military Commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 太和初，討李同捷，遷檢校戶部尚書、滄州刺史、滄德景節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign, when Li Tongjie was suppressed, he was transferred to Acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Cang Prefecture, and Military Commissioner of Cang, De, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Taihe reign, during the campaign against Li Tongjie, he was made Acting Minister of Revenue, Prefect of Cang, and Military Commissioner of Cang, De, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 太和三年五月卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth month of the third year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 董重質，本淮西牙將，吳少誠之子婿也。

translations.literal: Dong Chongzhi was originally a garrison officer of Huaixi and the son-in-law of Wu Shaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi had been a garrison officer in Huaixi and was married to a daughter of Wu Shaoqing.

sentences.zh: 性勇悍，識軍機，善用兵。

translations.literal: By nature he was fierce and bold, understood military affairs, and was skilled in the use of troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature fierce and resolute, understood the machinery of war, and knew how to command men.

sentences.zh: 及元濟拒命，重質又為謀主，領大軍當王師，連歲不拔，皆重質之謀也。

translations.literal: When Yuanji defied orders, Chongzhi again became the chief strategist, leading the main army to confront the imperial forces; for years they could not be dislodged, and this was all due to Chongzhi's plans.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji rebelled, Chongzhi again became chief strategist, leading the main force against the imperial armies. Year after year the government could not break them—and year after year, the reason was Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年，宰相裴度督兵淮西，至郾城，元濟乃悉發左右及守城之卒，委重質而拒度。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, the Chancellor Pei Du supervised the Huaixi campaign; when he reached Yancheng, Yuanji then sent out all his personal followers and the troops defending the city, entrusting them to Chongzhi to resist Du.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe, Chancellor Pei Du took command of the Huaixi campaign. When he reached Yancheng, Yuanji emptied the city of his personal guard and garrison troops and put them all under Chongzhi to hold Du at bay.

sentences.zh: 時李愬乘虛入蔡。

translations.literal: At that time Li Su seized the opening and entered Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Li Su slipped through the gap and entered Cai.

sentences.zh: 既擒元濟，重質之家在蔡，愬乃安恤之，仍使其子持書禮以召重質。

translations.literal: After Yuanji was captured, Chongzhi's family were in Cai; Su then reassured and comforted them, and still had his son carry a letter and gifts to summon Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuanji was taken, Su learned that Chongzhi's family were still in Cai. He saw to their safety and sent Chongzhi's son with a letter and gifts to call him in.

sentences.zh: 重質見其子，知城已陷，及元濟囚窘之狀，乃慨然以單騎歸愬，白衣叩伏。

translations.literal: When Chongzhi saw his son, he knew the city had fallen and saw Yuanji's imprisoned and distressed condition; he then, filled with emotion, returned alone on horseback to Su, dressed in white and prostrating himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhi met his son and learned that the city had fallen—and saw Yuanji broken and in chains—he rode alone to Su in plain clothes and threw himself face down before him.

sentences.zh: 愬揖登階，以賓禮與之食。

translations.literal: Su bowed and had him ascend the steps, treating him with the rites due a guest and sharing a meal with him.
translations.idiomatic: Su raised him with a bow, led him up the steps, and received him as an honored guest at table.

sentences.zh: 憲宗欲殺之，愬奏許以不死而來降，請免之，且乞於本軍驅使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong wished to kill him, but Su memorialized that he had promised him he would not die if he came to surrender, and asked that his life be spared and that he be allowed to serve in Su's own army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong wanted him executed, but Su argued that he had promised Chongzhi his life in return for surrender, begged that the promise be kept, and asked to employ him in his own command.

sentences.zh: 於是，貶春州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was demoted to Registrar of Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon demoted him to Registrar of Chun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉太子少詹事，委武寧軍收管驅使，仍加金紫。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent, placed under the control and service of the Wuning Army, and additionally granted the gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Junior Steward of the Heir Apparent, assigned to the Wuning Army for service, and honored with the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 十五年，征入，授左神武軍將軍，知軍事，兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned [to court] and appointed General of the Left Divine Martial Army, with charge of military affairs, and concurrently Censor Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was recalled and made General of the Left Divine Martial Army with charge of military affairs, while also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 仍賜金帛，與有功者等。

translations.literal: He was again granted gold and silk, equal to those who had earned merit.
translations.idiomatic: He received gold and silk as well, the same reward given to men of proven merit.

sentences.zh: 尋授鹽州刺史，又遷左右神策及諸道劍南西川行營節度使、檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Prefect of Yan Prefecture, then transferred again to Left and Right Divine Strategy [Army commander] and Military Commissioner of the Xichuan Expeditionary Camp in Jiannan, and Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Prefect of Yan, then transferred to command the Left and Right Divine Strategy Armies and the Xichuan expedition in Jiannan, with the additional title of Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，又轉夏綏銀宥節度使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was again transferred to Military Commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he was again transferred to Military Commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.

sentences.zh: 五年，就加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he received the additional title of Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 重質訓兵立法，羌戎畏服。

translations.literal: Chongzhi trained troops and established laws; the Qiang and Rong feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhi drilled his soldiers and set firm regulations, and the Qiang and Rong tribes feared and obeyed him.

sentences.zh: 八年八月卒，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eighth year he died, and was posthumously granted the title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth month of the eighth year and was posthumously honored as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 楊元卿，祖子華，德州安陵縣丞。

translations.literal: Yang Yuanqing's grandfather Zihua was Assistant Magistrate of Anling County in De Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanqing's grandfather Zihua had served as Assistant Magistrate of Anling County in De Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父寓，申州鐘山縣令。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Magistrate of Zhongshan County in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had been Magistrate of Zhongshan County in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元卿少孤，慷慨有才略。

translations.literal: Yuanqing was orphaned young, but was generous in spirit and possessed talent and stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing lost his father early, yet he grew up open-handed and sharp-minded.

sentences.zh: 及冠，尚漂蕩江嶺之表，縱遊放言，人謂之狂生。

translations.literal: When he came of age he still drifted about the lands south of the Yangzi and the mountain ranges, wandering freely and speaking boldly; people called him a wild youth.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he came of age he roamed the river lands and southern hills, speaking whatever came to mind. People called him a wild young man.

sentences.zh: 時吳少誠專蔡州，朝廷姑息之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Shaoqing controlled Cai Prefecture, and the court indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Shaoqing held Cai Prefecture in his grip, and the court chose to appease him.

sentences.zh: 元卿白衣謁見，署以劇縣，旋辟為從事，奏授試大理評事。

translations.literal: Yuanqing visited him in plain clothes, was appointed to a demanding county post, and was soon recruited as an aide; he was memorialized and granted the probationary post of Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing came to him unarmed and unadorned, was given a hard county to govern, and was soon taken on as an aide. A memorial secured him the probationary post of Assessor of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 亦事少陽，後奏轉監察裏行。

translations.literal: He also served Wu Shaoyang, and was later memorialized and transferred to Acting Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later served Wu Shaoyang as well and was eventually promoted by memorial to Acting Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 因上奏，宰相李吉甫深加慰納，自是一歲或再隨奏至京師。

translations.literal: Because he submitted memorials [to court], Chancellor Li Jifu deeply welcomed and accepted him; from then on, once or twice a year he would follow his memorials to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials reached the capital, and Chancellor Li Jifu welcomed him warmly. After that he traveled to the capital once or twice a year with each round of submissions.

sentences.zh: 元卿每與少陽言，諭以大義。

translations.literal: Yuanqing often spoke with Shaoyang, instructing him in the greater principles of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing often spoke with Shaoyang, trying to turn him with the language of loyalty and larger obligation.

sentences.zh: 乃為兇黨所構，賴節度判官蘇肇保持，故免。

translations.literal: He was then framed by the violent faction; only because the military commissioner's aide Su Zhao protected him was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel hardliners then plotted against him, and he survived only because the commissioner's aide Su Zhao shielded him.

sentences.zh: 元卿潛奉朝廷，內耗少陽之事。

translations.literal: Yuanqing secretly served the court, draining Shaoyang's affairs from within.
translations.idiomatic: In secret Yuanqing served the court, weakening Shaoyang's power from within.

sentences.zh: 及少陽死，其子元濟繼立。

translations.literal: When Shaoyang died, his son Yuanji succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaoyang died, his son Yuanji took his place.

sentences.zh: 元卿說曰：「先尚書性吝，諸將皆饑寒。

translations.literal: Yuanqing persuaded him, saying: "Your late father was by nature stingy, and all the generals were hungry and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing urged him, saying, "Your father was miserly by nature, and the generals have gone hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 今須布惠以自固也。

translations.literal: Now you must distribute favors in order to secure yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to hold your position, you must win them with generosity.

sentences.zh: 府中有無，元卿熟知之，曷若散聘諸道，卑辭厚禮，以丈人行呼群帥，庶幾一助，而諸將大獲矣。

translations.literal: Whether the prefectural treasury has resources or not, Yuanqing knows it thoroughly—would it not be better to send envoys to the various circuits, with humble words and generous gifts, addressing the commanders as elders? Perhaps you may gain some aid, and the generals will profit greatly.
translations.idiomatic: I know exactly what the treasury holds and what it lacks. Why not send envoys to the other circuits with humble words and rich gifts, treating their commanders as elders? You may win some outside help, and the generals will feast.

sentences.zh: 元卿願將留後表上聞，朝廷安得不從哉？」

translations.literal: Yuanqing is willing to carry the regent's memorial to the throne—how could the court refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Let me carry your regent's memorial to the throne. The court will hardly refuse."

sentences.zh: 元濟許之。

translations.literal: Yuanji agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji agreed.

sentences.zh: 元卿即日離蔡，以賊勢盈虛條奏，潛請詔諸道拘留使者。

translations.literal: Yuanqing left Cai that very day, memorialized item by item on the rebels' strength and weakness, and secretly requested an edict that the various circuits detain the envoys.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Yuanqing left Cai. He sent up a detailed report on the rebels' strengths and weaknesses and secretly asked the throne to order every circuit to detain the envoys.

sentences.zh: 及元濟覺，元卿妻陳氏並四男並為元濟所殺，同圬一射垛。

translations.literal: When Yuanji realized what had happened, Yuanqing's wife Lady Chen and four sons were all killed by Yuanji and buried together in one rampart of earth.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanji discovered the betrayal, he killed Yuanqing's wife Lady Chen and their four sons and heaped them into a single grave mound.

sentences.zh: 蘇肇以保持元卿，亦同日被害。

translations.literal: Su Zhao, because he had protected Yuanqing, was killed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhao, who had shielded Yuanqing, was killed that same day.

sentences.zh: 詔授元卿嶽王府司馬，尋遷太子僕射。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yuanqing Assistant Master of the Yue Royal Household; he was soon promoted to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The throne appointed Yuanqing Assistant Master of the Yue Royal Household, and soon promoted him to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Palace.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，授蔡州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was appointed Prefect of Cai and concurrently Censor Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he was made Prefect of Cai and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 未行，改授光祿少卿。

translations.literal: Before he departed, the appointment was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Brightness Office.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the appointment was changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Brightness Office.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷比令元卿與李愬會議，於唐州東境選要便處，權置行蔡州。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had repeatedly ordered Yuanqing and Li Su to confer and, on the eastern border of Tang Prefecture, choose a strategic location where a provisional Cai Prefecture might be established.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had ordered Yuanqing and Li Su to meet and, on Tang Prefecture's eastern frontier, choose a defensible site for a provisional Cai government.

sentences.zh: 如百姓官健有歸順者，便準敕優恤，必令全活。

translations.literal: If any civilians or soldiers wished to surrender, they were to be treated with favor according to the edict, so that their lives would certainly be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Any civilian or soldier who came over was to be treated generously under imperial decree and kept alive.

sentences.zh: 既而召見，元卿遽奏請借度支錢，及言事頗多不合旨。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was summoned to audience; Yuanqing hastily memorialized to borrow funds from the Department of Public Works, and what he said on other matters largely failed to accord with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to court, Yuanqing immediately asked to borrow funds from the treasury and spoke at length on matters the emperor did not wish to hear.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴度亦以諸將討賊三年，功成在旦暮，如更分土地與元卿，即恐相侵生事，故罷前命而改授焉。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pei Du also thought that the generals had campaigned against the rebels for three years and success was imminent; if land were further divided and given to Yuanqing, he feared encroachment and trouble would arise, and so the earlier order was revoked and the new appointment made.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pei Du also reasoned that after three years of war success was near; granting Yuanqing his own territory now would only breed friction and fresh trouble. The earlier commission was withdrawn and he was given another post instead.

sentences.zh: 是歲，既平淮西，元卿奏曰：「淮西甚有寶貨及犀帶，臣知之，往取必得。」

translations.literal: That year, once Huaixi was pacified, Yuanqing memorialized, saying: "Huaixi has great stores of treasure, goods, and rhinoceros-horn belts—I know this, and if I go to take them I am sure to obtain them."
translations.idiomatic: That year, after Huaixi fell, Yuanqing memorialized: "There is great wealth in Huaixi—treasure, goods, rhinoceros-horn belts. I know where it lies, and if sent I can bring it back."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕本討賊，為人除害，今賊平人安，則我求之得矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'I originally campaigned against the rebels to remove harm for the people. Now that the rebels are pacified and the people are at peace, what I sought has already been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, 'I raised this army to destroy evil and save the people. The rebels are broken and the land is at peace—that is the victory I wanted.

sentences.zh: 寶貨犀帶，非所求也，勿復此言。」

translations.literal: Treasure, goods, and rhinoceros-horn belts are not what I seek—do not speak of this again.'
translations.idiomatic: Treasure and rhinoceros belts are not what I seek. Do not raise this again.'

sentences.zh: 是月，詔授左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: That month an edict appointed him General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: That month an edict made him General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改汾州刺史，復征為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Prefect of Fen Prefecture, then recalled again as General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent out as Prefect of Fen, then recalled once more as General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，易置鎮、魏守臣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing reign the defenders of Zhen and Wei were replaced.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Changqing reign the court reshuffled the commanders of Zhen and Wei.

sentences.zh: 元卿詣宰相深陳利害，並具表其事。

translations.literal: Yuanqing went to the chancellors and explained the advantages and harms in depth, and also submitted a detailed memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing went before the chancellors, laid out the risks at length, and submitted a full memorial on the subject.

sentences.zh: 後穆宗感悟，賜白玉帶，旋授檢校左散騎常侍、涇州刺史、涇原渭節度觀察等使，兼充四鎮北庭行軍。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Muzong came to understand, granted him a white jade belt, and soon appointed him Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Prefect of Jing Prefecture, Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Jingyuan and Wei, while also serving as commander of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expeditionary force.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong eventually saw the wisdom of it, granted him a white jade belt, and soon made him Acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, Prefect of Jing, Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Jingyuan and Wei, and commander of the Four Garrisons and Northern Court expedition.

sentences.zh: 元卿乃奏置屯田五千頃，每屯築墻高數仞，鍵閉牢密，卒然寇至，盡可保守。

translations.literal: Yuanqing then memorialized to establish five thousand qing of military colonies; each colony would build walls several ren high, locked and sealed tight, so that if raiders suddenly arrived, all could be defended and held.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing then proposed five thousand qing of frontier farms, each settlement walled several ren high and sealed tight, so that sudden raids could be weathered and every store of grain preserved.

sentences.zh: 加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He received the additional title of Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 營田成，復加使號。

translations.literal: When the military farms were completed, his commission title was further enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: When the farms were finished, his commission was expanded again.

sentences.zh: 居六年，涇人論奏，為立德政碑，移授懷州刺史，充河陽三城節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: After six years in office, the people of Jing submitted a memorial and had a stele erected to his virtuous governance; he was transferred to Prefect of Huai Prefecture and made Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: After six years the people of Jing petitioned the throne and raised a stele to his good rule. He was then transferred to Huai as prefect and made Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，就加檢校司空，進階光祿大夫，以其營田納粟二十萬石，以裨經費故也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he was additionally appointed Acting Grand Master of Works, promoted in rank to Grand Master of Imperial Brightness, because his military farms had delivered two hundred thousand shi of grain to supplement state expenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he was further honored as Acting Grand Master of Works and promoted to Grand Master of Imperial Brightness, in recognition of the two hundred thousand shi of grain his farms had delivered to the treasury.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改授汴宋亳觀察等使。

translations.literal: That year he was reassigned as Observation Commissioner of Bian, Song, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was reassigned as Observation Commissioner of Bian, Song, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 凡所廢置，皆有弘益，詔並從之。

translations.literal: Every abolition and establishment he proposed brought broad benefit, and edicts approved them all.
translations.idiomatic: Every reform he proposed brought real benefit, and the throne approved them all.

sentences.zh: 年七十，寢疾，歸洛陽，詔授太子太保。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy he fell ill, returned to Luoyang, and was appointed by edict as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy he fell ill, returned to Luoyang, and was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是歲八月卒，廢朝三日，贈司徒。

translations.literal: That year, in the eighth month, he died; court audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously granted the title of Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year in the eighth month. Audiences were suspended for three days, and he was posthumously honored as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 元卿始以毀家效順，累授方鎮。

translations.literal: Yuanqing had begun by destroying his family to prove his loyalty, and was repeatedly appointed to regional commands.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing had first proved his loyalty by sacrificing his family, and rose through repeated appointments to command whole regions.

sentences.zh: 然性險巧，所至好聚斂，善結交，涇人得情，亦由此也。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was crafty and dangerous; wherever he went he loved to amass wealth, and he was skilled at forming alliances—the people of Jing came to favor him for this reason as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature cunning and grasping. Wherever he went he hoarded wealth and cultivated allies, and the people of Jing warmed to him for that reason too.

sentences.zh: 子延宗，開成中為磁州刺史，坐謀逐河陽節度使以自立，為其黨所告，臺司推鞫得實，誅之。

translations.literal: His son Yanzong, in the Kaicheng reign, was Prefect of Ci Prefecture; he was executed after plotting with others to drive out the Military Commissioner of Heyang and establish himself, was denounced by his own faction, was investigated by the censorial offices and found guilty, and was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzong served as Prefect of Ci in the Kaicheng reign. He plotted to oust the Military Commissioner of Heyang and rule in his stead, was betrayed by his own confederates, convicted after investigation by the censorial court, and executed.

sentences.zh: 劉悟，正臣之孫也。

translations.literal: Liu Wu was the grandson of Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu was the grandson of Liu Zhengchen.

sentences.zh: 正臣本名客奴。

translations.literal: Zhengchen's original name was Kenü.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchen had originally been named Kenü—Guest-Slave.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，祿山叛，平盧軍節度使柳知晦受賊偽署。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, Lushan rebelled; Liu Zhihui, military governor of the Pinglu Army, accepted a false commission from the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Tianbao reign, An Lushan rose in rebellion, and Liu Zhihui, military governor of the Pinglu Army, accepted a bogus appointment from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 客奴時職居牙門，襲殺知晦，馳章以聞。

translations.literal: Kenü then held a post in the yamen guard; he launched a surprise attack and killed Zhihui, then sent a dispatch at full speed to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Kenü, who then served in the headquarters guard, launched a surprise attack and killed Zhihui, then galloped off a memorial to report what he had done.

sentences.zh: 授平盧軍節度使，賜名正臣。

translations.literal: He was appointed military governor of the Pinglu Army and granted the name Zhengchen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Pinglu Army and given the honorific name Zhengchen—Righteous Minister.

sentences.zh: 悟少有勇力。

translations.literal: Wu in his youth possessed courage and strength.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Wu was known for his courage and physical prowess.

sentences.zh: 叔逸準為汴帥，積緡錢數百萬於洛中；

translations.literal: His uncle Yi Zhun was commander of Bian and had amassed several million strings of cash in Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yi Zhun, commander of Bian, had amassed several million strings of cash in Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 悟輒破扃鐍，悉盜用之。

translations.literal: Wu broke the locks and stole the whole sum for use.
translations.idiomatic: Wu broke open the locks and stole the entire hoard for his own use.

sentences.zh: 既而懼，亡歸李師古。

translations.literal: Then, fearing punishment, he fled and returned to Li Shigu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the consequences, he fled and took refuge with Li Shigu.

sentences.zh: 始亦未甚知，後因擊球馳突，沖師古馬仆，師古怒，將斬之。

translations.literal: At first Shigu did not think much of him; later, while playing polo and charging recklessly, he knocked Shigu's horse down. Shigu was angry and was about to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shigu thought little of him. Later, during a polo match, Wu charged recklessly and knocked Shigu from his horse. Shigu flew into a rage and was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 悟猛以氣語押觸師古，師古奇而免之。

translations.literal: Wu boldly spoke in a confrontational tone and pressed against Shigu; Shigu marveled and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu answered back boldly, pressing close with defiant words—and Shigu, struck by his spirit, let him live.

sentences.zh: 因令管壯士，將後軍，累署衙門右職，奏授淄青節度都知兵馬使、兼監察御史。

translations.literal: He was then put in charge of stalwart warriors and commanded the rearguard; he rose through successive right-hand posts in the headquarters and was memorialized for appointment as overall commander of Ziqing forces and concurrent censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu then put him in charge of picked fighting men and the rearguard. He rose through a series of senior headquarters posts until he was memorialized for appointment as overall commander of the Ziqing forces and concurrent censor.

sentences.zh: 元和末，憲宗既平淮西，下詔誅師道。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, after Emperor Xianzong had pacified Huai West, an edict was issued condemning Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era, after Emperor Xianzong had pacified the Huai West circuit, the throne issued an edict calling for Li Shidao's destruction.

sentences.zh: 遣悟將兵拒魏博軍，而數促悟戰。

translations.literal: Wu was sent to lead troops against the Weibo army, while Shidao repeatedly pressed him to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was dispatched to lead troops against the Weibo army, but Shidao repeatedly pressed him to give battle.

sentences.zh: 悟未及進，馳使召之。

translations.literal: Before Wu could advance, a messenger was sent at full speed to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu could advance, Shidao sent a courier at full gallop to summon him.

sentences.zh: 悟度使來必殺己，乃偽疾不出，令都虞候往迎之。

translations.literal: Wu judged that when the envoy came he would certainly be killed; he therefore feigned illness and did not go out, sending the chief adjutant to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu concluded that the envoy had come to kill him. He feigned illness and refused to go out, sending his chief adjutant to meet the messenger instead.

sentences.zh: 使者亦果以誠告其人，雲「奉命殺悟以代悟」。

translations.literal: The envoy indeed confided the truth to that man, saying, 'I am under orders to kill Wu and replace him with another.'
translations.idiomatic: The messenger did in fact confide the truth to the adjutant, saying, "I carry orders to kill Wu and put someone else in his place."

sentences.zh: 都虞候即時先還，悟劾之得其實，乃召諸將與謀曰：「魏博田弘正兵強，出戰必敗，不出則死。

translations.literal: The chief adjutant immediately returned ahead of him; Wu interrogated him and learned the facts, then summoned the officers and counseled them, saying: "Tian Hongzheng of Weibo has strong troops; if we go out to fight we are sure to lose, but if we do not go out we will die.
translations.idiomatic: The chief adjutant hurried back ahead of the envoy. Wu questioned him, learned the truth, and then summoned his officers to counsel with them, saying, "Tian Hongzheng of Weibo commands a powerful force. If we go out to fight, we are certain to be defeated; if we refuse, we die anyway.

sentences.zh: 今天子所誅者，司空一人而已，悟與公等皆為所驅迫，使就其死。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven seeks to punish only the Minister of Works; Wu and you gentlemen are all being driven and compelled to march toward your deaths.
translations.idiomatic: All the Son of Heaven truly wants is the Minister of Works himself. Wu and the rest of you are being driven forward only to die in his place.

sentences.zh: 何如殺其來使，整戈以取鄆，立大功，轉危亡為富貴耶！」

translations.literal: Why not kill their envoy, ready our weapons, and seize Yan—establish a great achievement and turn peril and ruin into wealth and honor!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not kill the envoy, take up our arms, and seize Yan for ourselves? We would win a great victory and turn disaster into wealth and honor!"

sentences.zh: 眾咸曰：「善，唯都將所命！」

translations.literal: All said: 'Excellent—we await only the commander's orders!'
translations.idiomatic: All cried out as one, "Well said! We await only our commander's word!"

sentences.zh: 悟於是立斬其使，以兵取鄆，圍其內城，兼以火攻其門。

translations.literal: Wu thereupon executed the envoy on the spot, seized Yan with troops, besieged the inner city, and also assaulted the gates with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Wu immediately executed the messenger, marched on Yan, besieged the inner city, and set fire to the gates.

sentences.zh: 不數刻，擒師道並男二人，並斬其首以獻。

translations.literal: Within scarcely a few quarters of an hour he captured Shidao together with two sons, and had all three beheaded and their heads presented.
translations.idiomatic: In less than an hour he captured Shidao together with two of his sons, beheaded all three, and sent their heads as trophies.

sentences.zh: 擢拜悟檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫、義成軍節度使，封彭城郡王，仍賜實封五百戶，錢二萬貫，莊、宅各一區。

translations.literal: Wu was promoted and appointed acting Minister of Works, concurrent Grand Censor, and military governor of the Yicheng Army; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng commandery, and moreover granted five hundred taxable households as permanent fief, twenty thousand strings of cash, and one estate and one residence each.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was promoted to acting Minister of Works, concurrent Grand Censor, and military governor of the Yicheng Army. He was enfeoffed as Prince of Pengcheng, granted five hundred households of permanent fief income, twenty thousand strings of cash, and one country estate and one city residence.

sentences.zh: 十五年正月入覲，又加檢校兵部尚書，余如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifteenth year he entered court for audience and was further made acting Minister of War; the rest remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifteenth year he came to court for an audience and was further made acting Minister of War; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，以恩例遷檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Wu was transferred by grace to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, Wu was transferred by imperial favor to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，移鎮澤潞，旋以本官兼平章事。

translations.literal: That same year in the tenth month he was transferred to defend Zelu; shortly thereafter he received his existing rank concurrent with Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the tenth month, he was transferred to command at Zelu-Lu, and shortly afterward was given his existing rank together with the title of Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年，幽州大將硃克融叛，囚其帥張弘靖，朝廷求名將以鎮漁陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changqing, the great general Zhu Kerong of Youzhou rebelled and imprisoned his commander Zhang Hongjing; the court sought a renowned commander to secure Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Changqing era, the Youzhou general Zhu Kerong rebelled and imprisoned his commander Zhang Hongjing. The court searched for a celebrated general to secure Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 乃加悟檢校司空、平章事，充盧龍軍節度使。

translations.literal: Wu was then promoted to acting Grand Master of Works and Grand Councillor and appointed military governor of the Lulong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was accordingly promoted to acting Grand Master of Works and Grand Councillor, and appointed military governor of the Lulong Army.

sentences.zh: 悟以幽州方亂，未克進討，請授之節鉞，徐圖之。

translations.literal: Wu, judging Youzhou to be in turmoil and unable to be immediately suppressed, requested that the military commission be granted to him so he might proceed gradually.
translations.idiomatic: Wu judged that Youzhou was still in turmoil and could not be subdued at once. He asked that the command be granted to him so he might take it in hand gradually.

sentences.zh: 乃復以悟為澤潞節度，拜檢校司徒，兼太子太傅，依前平章事。

translations.literal: He was then again made military governor of Zelu, appointed acting Grand Preceptor, concurrent Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and retained as before as Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The court then restored him as military governor of Zelu, appointed him acting Grand Preceptor and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and left him in place as Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 時監軍劉承偕頗恃恩權，常對眾辱悟；

translations.literal: At the time the army supervisor Liu Chengjie relied heavily on imperial favor and power, and often humiliated Wu before the assembled troops;
translations.idiomatic: At the time the army supervisor Liu Chengjie leaned heavily on imperial favor and often humiliated Wu before the assembled troops;

sentences.zh: 又縱其下亂法，悟不能平。

translations.literal: he also allowed his subordinates to violate regulations with impunity, and Wu could not keep order.
translations.idiomatic: he also let his subordinates break the law at will, and Wu could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 異日有中使至，承偕宴之，請悟，悟欲往。

translations.literal: On another day when a palace envoy arrived, Chengjie hosted a banquet for him and invited Wu; Wu intended to go.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion a palace envoy arrived. Chengjie gave him a banquet and invited Wu to attend. Wu meant to go.

sentences.zh: 左右皆曰：「往則必為其困辱矣！」

translations.literal: His attendants all said: "If you go you will surely suffer insult and humiliation at their hands!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants all said, "If you go, they are sure to trap and humiliate you!"

sentences.zh: 軍眾因亂，悟不止之。

translations.literal: The troops thereupon fell into disorder, and Wu did not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The troops thereupon broke into disorder, and Wu made no move to stop them.

sentences.zh: 乃擒承偕至牙門，殺其二仆，欲並害承偕，悟救之獲免。

translations.literal: They seized Chengjie and brought him to the headquarters gate, killed his two servants, and were about to kill Chengjie as well; Wu rescued him and he escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Chengjie and dragged him to the headquarters gate, killed his two attendants, and were about to kill Chengjie himself. Wu intervened and saved him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不獲已，貶承偕。

translations.literal: The court, having no alternative, demoted Chengjie.
translations.idiomatic: The court, left with no good choice, demoted Chengjie.

sentences.zh: 自是悟頗縱恣，欲效河朔三鎮。

translations.literal: From this point Wu grew quite unrestrained, seeking to emulate the three Hebei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Wu grew increasingly lawless, seeking to imitate the three Hebei circuits.

sentences.zh: 朝廷失意不逞之徒，多投寄潞州以求援。

translations.literal: Those in the capital who had lost favor and could not achieve their ambitions often took refuge in Luzhou to seek support.
translations.idiomatic: Men in the capital who had fallen from favor and could not get their way often fled to Luzhou to seek Wu's protection.

sentences.zh: 往往奏章論事，辭旨不遜。

translations.literal: They frequently submitted memorials on affairs of state, their language disrespectful and insubordinate.
translations.idiomatic: They repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs, their language insolent and defiant.

sentences.zh: 寶歷元年九月病卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Baoli he died of illness; posthumously he was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the first year of the Baoli era he died of illness. He was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 遺表請以其子從諫繼纘戎事。

translations.literal: In his final memorial he asked that his son Congjian succeed to command of the military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his deathbed memorial he asked that his son Liu Congjian succeed him in command of the army.

sentences.zh: 敬宗下大臣議。

translations.literal: Emperor Jingzong referred the matter to his chief ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jingzong referred the request to his chief ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 僕射李絳以澤潞內地，與三鎮事理不同，不可許。

translations.literal: Vice Director Li Jiang argued that Zelu lay in the interior and differed in principle from the Three Circuits; the request could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Li Jiang argued that Zelu-Lu lay in the interior and was fundamentally unlike the three Hebei circuits; the request ought not be granted.

sentences.zh: 宰相李逢吉、中尉王守澄受其賂，曲為奏請。

translations.literal: Chancellor Li Fengji and the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng accepted bribes from them and distorted the matter in their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Li Fengji and the chief eunuch Wang Shoucheng accepted bribes from the Liu family and twisted their memorial into a favorable recommendation.

sentences.zh: 從諫自將作監主簿，起復雲麾將軍，守金吾衛大將軍同正、檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史大夫，充昭義節度副大使，知節度觀察等留後。

translations.literal: Congjian rose from Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings; recalled from mourning as General of the Cloud-Banner Guard; appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant; concurrent Censor-in-Chief; deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi; and acting inspector of the circuit and related duties.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was recalled from mourning from his post as Master Recorder in the Directorate for Palace Buildings, appointed General of the Cloud-Banner Guard, Acting Left Regular Attendant, and Censor-in-Chief, and made deputy military commissioner of Zhaoyi with acting authority over the circuit and related duties.

sentences.zh: 二年，加金吾上將軍、檢校工部尚書，充昭義節度等使。

translations.literal: In the second year he was given Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Senior General of the Golden Guard, Acting Minister of Works, and full military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，進檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong acceded, he was advanced to Acting Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Congjian was promoted to Acting Sikong.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月入覲。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he came to court.

sentences.zh: 七年春歸籓，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his post and was given Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he returned to his command and was made Concurrent Associate Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 九年，李訓事敗，宰相王涯等四人被禍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Li Xun affair failed; Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year the Li Xun plot failed, and Grand Councilor Wang Ya and three others were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 時涯兼掌邦計，雖不與李訓同謀，然不自異於其間，既死非其罪。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Ya also oversaw state finance; though he had not conspired with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his death was not deserved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was then also in charge of state finance. Though he had not plotted with Li Xun, he had not kept himself apart from the affair, and his execution was undeserved.

sentences.zh: 從諫素德涯之私恩，心頗不平，四上章請涯等罪名，仇士良輩深憚之。

translations.literal: Congjian had long owed Wang Ya a personal debt of gratitude and was quite unsettled in mind; four times he submitted memorials asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed; Qiu Shiliang and his faction deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian had long felt a personal debt to Wang Ya and was deeply troubled by the case. Four times he memorialized asking what crimes Wang Ya and the others had committed. Qiu Shiliang and his faction feared him greatly.

sentences.zh: 是時中官頗橫，天子不能制。

translations.literal: At that time eunuch officials were quite overbearing and the emperor could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuch officials were rampant, and the emperor could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 朝臣日憂陷族，賴從諫論列，而鄭覃、李石方能粗秉朝政。

translations.literal: Court officials daily feared the extermination of their clans; they relied on Congjian's forthright memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials lived in daily fear that their entire clans would be wiped out. They depended on Congjian's outspoken memorials, and only then could Zheng Tan and Li Shi roughly hold the reins of government.

sentences.zh: 先是，有蕭洪者，詐稱太后弟，因仇士良保任，許之厚賂。

translations.literal: Previously there was a man named Xiao Hong who falsely claimed to be the Empress Dowager's younger brother; through Qiu Shiliang's protection and appointment he had promised lavish bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been a man named Xiao Hong who falsely claimed to be the Empress Dowager's younger brother. With Qiu Shiliang's protection and patronage, he had promised lavish bribes.

sentences.zh: 及洪累授方鎮，納賂不滿士良之誌，士良怒，遣人上書論洪非太后之親，又以蕭本者為太后弟。

translations.literal: When Hong was repeatedly appointed to regional commands but his bribes failed to satisfy Shiliang's desires, Shiliang grew angry and sent someone to submit a memorial arguing that Hong was not the Empress Dowager's kin, and claimed instead that a certain Xiao Ben was her younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong received one regional appointment after another yet failed to pay bribes large enough to satisfy Shiliang, Shiliang grew furious. He had someone submit a memorial declaring that Hong was not the Empress Dowager's kinsman, and naming a certain Xiao Ben as her true younger brother instead.

sentences.zh: 從諫深知內宮之故，乃自潞府飛章論之曰：「臣聞造偽以亂真者，匹夫知之尚不可，況天下皆知乎？

translations.literal: Congjian knew well the inner-palace background; from his post at Luzhou he submitted an urgent memorial arguing: "Your subject has heard that to manufacture falsehood to confuse truth—even a common man who knows this finds it intolerable; how much more when all the realm knows it?
translations.idiomatic: Congjian knew the inner-palace intrigue behind the affair. From Luzhou he sent an urgent memorial, writing: "I have heard that to manufacture falsehood and confuse what is true is something even a common man, once he knows of it, cannot abide—how much less when all the realm knows?

sentences.zh: 執疏以為親者，在匹夫之家尚不可，況處大國之朝乎？

translations.literal: To cling to a petition claiming kinship—even in a commoner's household this is intolerable; how much more in the court of a great state?
translations.idiomatic: To cling to a written claim of kinship is intolerable even in a commoner's household—how much more in the court of a great empire?

sentences.zh: 臣受國恩深，奉公心切，知有此失，安敢不言！

translations.literal: Your subject has received deep grace from the state and serves the public with earnest heart; knowing this error, how dare he remain silent!
translations.idiomatic: I have received deep grace from the state and serve the public with all my heart. Knowing this wrong, how dare I remain silent!

sentences.zh: 伏唯皇帝陛下仁及萬方，孝敦九族，而推心無黨，唯理是求。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty's benevolence reaches all directions, your filial devotion nourishes the nine kin, and you extend your heart without faction, seeking only what is right.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's benevolence reaches every corner of the realm, your filial devotion embraces the nine degrees of kin, and you govern with an open heart, free of faction, seeking only what is right.

sentences.zh: 微臣所以不避直言，切論深事。

translations.literal: That is why this humble subject does not shrink from blunt speech and urgently addresses this grave matter.
translations.idiomatic: That is why I do not shrink from blunt speech in urgently addressing this grave matter.

sentences.zh: 伏見金吾將軍蕭本，稱是太后親弟，受此官榮。

translations.literal: I respectfully observe that General of the Golden Crow Guard Xiao Ben claims to be the Empress Dowager's own younger brother and has received this honor and glory.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that General of the Golden Crow Guard Xiao Ben claims to be the Empress Dowager's own younger brother and has received rank and honor on that basis.

sentences.zh: 今喧然國都，迨聞籓府，自上及下，異口同音，皆言蕭弘是真，蕭本是偽。

translations.literal: Now it resounds through the capital and reaches every regional command; from highest to lowest, all speak with one voice, saying Xiao Hong is genuine and Xiao Ben is false.
translations.idiomatic: Now the uproar fills the capital and reaches every regional command. From highest to lowest, all speak with one voice: Xiao Hong is the true kinsman; Xiao Ben is the impostor.

sentences.zh: 臣傍聽眾論，遍察群情，鹹思發明，以正名分。

translations.literal: Your subject has listened beside the crowd to public discussion and broadly examined the sentiments of all, and earnestly wishes to bring the truth to light to set right names and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Having listened to public discussion and weighed the mood of the court and the realm, I earnestly wish to bring the truth to light and set names and ranks right.

sentences.zh: 今年二月，其蕭弘投臣當道，求臣上聞，自言：比者福建觀察使唐扶及監軍劉行立具審根源，已曾論奏。

translations.literal: This second month, Xiao Hong came to your subject's jurisdiction, asking that I report upward; he himself stated: recently Fujian observation commissioner Tang Fu and army supervisor Liu Xingli thoroughly investigated the origins and had already submitted memorials on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: This second month Xiao Hong came to my jurisdiction and asked me to report upward. He stated that Fujian observation commissioner Tang Fu and army supervisor Liu Xingli had already traced the matter to its roots and submitted memorials on it.

sentences.zh: 其時屬蕭本得為外戚，來自左軍，臺司既不敢研窮，聖意遂勒還鄉里。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Ben had become an imperial affinal kinsman, backed by the Left Army; the censorate dared not pursue the investigation to the end, and by imperial decision he was ordered to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiao Ben had already become an imperial affinal kinsman with backing from the Left Army. The censorate did not dare pursue the investigation to the end, and by imperial order he was sent back to his home district.

sentences.zh: 自茲議論，轉益沸騰。

translations.literal: Since then discussion has grown ever more tumultuous.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the controversy has only grown more heated.

sentences.zh: 臣亦令潛問左軍，榷論大體，而士良推至公之道，發不黨之言。

translations.literal: Your subject also had inquiries made discreetly in the Left Army, weighing the broad principles, and Shiliang upheld the way of utmost fairness and spoke without partiality.
translations.idiomatic: I also made discreet inquiries in the Left Army and weighed the broader principles. Shiliang upheld the way of utmost fairness and spoke without partiality.

sentences.zh: 蓋蕭本自度孤危，妄有憑恃。

translations.literal: Presumably Xiao Ben, judging himself isolated and imperiled, presumptuously sought something to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Surely Xiao Ben, finding himself isolated and imperiled, presumptuously sought something to lean on.

sentences.zh: 伏以名居國舅，位列朝班，而真偽不分，中外所恥。

translations.literal: I respectfully submit: to hold the name of imperial maternal uncle and a seat in the court ranks, yet leave authenticity undistinguished—this is shameful at court and abroad alike.
translations.idiomatic: To bear the title of imperial maternal uncle and sit in the ranks of court, yet leave truth and falsehood undistinguished—this shames the court before all within and without.

sentences.zh: 切慮皇太后受此罔惑，已有恩情，若含垢於一時，終取笑於千古。

translations.literal: I deeply fear that the Empress Dowager, deceived by this fraud, has already formed emotional ties; if she endures shame for a moment, she will ultimately be mocked for a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: I deeply fear that the Empress Dowager, deceived by this fraud, has already formed ties of affection. If she swallows this disgrace for the moment, she will be mocked for a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 伏乞追蕭弘赴闕，與蕭本對推，細詰根源，必辨真偽。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg that Xiao Hong be summoned to court, confronted with Xiao Ben for joint examination, and the origins closely interrogated to determine truth and falsehood with certainty."
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg that Xiao Hong be summoned to court, confronted with Xiao Ben, and the origins examined in detail until truth and falsehood are settled beyond doubt."

sentences.zh: 詔令三司使推按。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the commissioners of the three offices to investigate and adjudicate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the commissioners of the Three Offices to investigate and adjudicate the case.

sentences.zh: 帝以二蕭雖詐，托名太后之宗，不欲誅之，俱流嶺表。

translations.literal: The Emperor, though both Xias were deceitful in claiming kinship with the Empress Dowager's clan, did not wish to execute them; both were banished to the Ling region.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, though both Xiao men had lied by claiming kinship with the Empress Dowager's clan, did not wish to put them to death. Both were banished to the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 從諫進位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Congjian was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 會昌三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Huichang era.

sentences.zh: 大將郭誼等匿喪，用其侄稹權領軍務。

translations.literal: The great generals Guo Yi and others concealed his death and had his nephew Zhen provisionally take command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The generals Guo Yi and others concealed his death and had his nephew Liu Zhen provisionally take command of the army.

sentences.zh: 時宰相李德裕用事，素惡從諫之奸回，奏請劉稹護喪歸洛，以聽朝旨。

translations.literal: At the time Chancellor Li Deyu held power and had long detested Congjian's devious conduct; he memorialized requesting Liu Zhen escort the bier back to Luoyang to await the court's orders.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chancellor Li Deyu held power and had long despised Congjian's treacherous ways. He memorialized asking that Liu Zhen escort the bier back to Luoyang and await the court's orders.

sentences.zh: 稹竟叛。

translations.literal: Zhen ultimately rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rebelled in the end.

sentences.zh: 德裕用中丞李回奉使河朔，說令三鎮加兵討稹；

translations.literal: Deyu employed Censor-in-Chief Li Hui on a mission to Hebei, persuading the Three Circuits to reinforce their troops against Zhen;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu dispatched Censor-in-Chief Li Hui on a mission to Hebei to persuade the three circuits to send additional troops against Zhen;

sentences.zh: 乃削奪稹官，命徐許滑孟魏鎮幽并八鎮之師，四面進攻。

translations.literal: Zhen's offices were then stripped, and forces from the eight circuits—Xu, Xu, Hua, Meng, Wei, Zhen, You, and Bing—were ordered to attack from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's offices were then stripped away, and armies from the eight circuits—Xu, Xu, Hua, Meng, Wei, Zhen, You, and Bing—were ordered to advance against him from every side.

sentences.zh: 四年，郭誼斬稹，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Guo Yi beheaded Zhen and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Guo Yi executed Zhen and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 從諫妻裴氏。

translations.literal: Congjian's wife was Lady Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Congjian's wife was Lady Pei.

sentences.zh: 初，稹拒命，裴氏召集大將妻同宴，以酒為壽，泣下不能已。

translations.literal: Initially, when Zhen defied orders, Lady Pei gathered the wives of the great generals for a banquet, offered wine in toasts, and wept without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen first defied the court's orders, Lady Pei summoned the generals' wives to a banquet, raised wine in toast, and wept without stopping.

sentences.zh: 諸婦請命，裴曰：「新婦各與汝夫文字，勿忘先相公之拔擢，莫效李丕背恩，走投國家。

translations.literal: The women asked what troubled her; Lady Pei said: 'Each of you newly wed wives shall give your husbands written words: do not forget how the late prime minister raised you up; do not follow Li Pi in betraying kindness and fleeing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: The women asked what ailed her. Lady Pei said, "Each of you, take written words to your husbands: do not forget how the late prime minister raised you up. Do not follow Li Pi in betraying past kindness and going over to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 子母為托，故悲不能已也。」

translations.literal: It is for my son and his mother that I entrust this message—hence my grief cannot cease."
translations.idiomatic: I weep because I entrust my son and his mother to you—that is why my grief will not cease."

sentences.zh: 諸婦亦泣下，故潞將叛誌益堅。

translations.literal: The women also wept, and thus the Lu generals' resolve to rebel grew firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: The women wept as well, and the Lu generals' resolve to rebel grew all the firmer.

sentences.zh: 稹死，裴亦以此極刑。

translations.literal: When Zhen died, Lady Pei also suffered extreme punishment for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was killed, Lady Pei too was punished with the utmost severity for this.

sentences.zh: 稹族屬昆仲九人，皆誅。

translations.literal: Nine brothers among Zhen's clan and kin were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Nine brothers among Zhen's clan were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 劉沔，許州牙將也。

translations.literal: Liu Mian was a yamen general of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was a headquarters officer of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少事李光顏為帳中親將。

translations.literal: In youth he served Li Guangyan as a personal officer in his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Li Guangyan as a personal officer on his staff.

sentences.zh: 元和末，光顏討吳元濟，常用沔為前鋒。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, when Guangyan campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he often used Mian as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe era, when Guangyan campaigned against Wu Yuanji, he regularly used Mian as his vanguard.

sentences.zh: 蔡將有董重質者，守洄曲，其部下乘騾即戰，號「騾子軍」，最為勁悍，官軍常警備之。

translations.literal: Among Cai's generals was Dong Chongzhi, defending Huaiqu; his subordinates fought mounted on mules, called the "Mule Cavalry," the fiercest of all—government troops were always on alert against them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the Cai generals was Dong Chongzhi, who held Huaiqu. His men fought mounted on mules and were called the "Mule Army"—the fiercest force of all, against whom the imperial troops were always on guard.

sentences.zh: 沔驍銳善騎射，每與騾軍接戰，必冒刃陷堅，俘馘而還，故忠武一軍，破賊第一。

translations.literal: Mian was fierce, elite, and skilled at mounted archery; whenever he engaged the Mule Army he always braved blades to break strong points, capturing heads and returning—thus within the Zhongwu army he ranked first in defeating the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was bold, sharp, and skilled in mounted archery. Whenever he clashed with the Mule Army he plunged through blade and wall, took heads, and returned victorious. In the Zhongwu army he ranked first in breaking the enemy.

sentences.zh: 淮、蔡平，隨光顏入朝。

translations.literal: When Huai and Cai were pacified, he entered court with Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai and Cai were pacified, he entered the capital with Guangyan.

sentences.zh: 憲宗留宿衛，歷三將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong retained him in the palace guard, where he rose through three generalships.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong kept him in the palace guard, where he rose through three generalships.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽州刺史、天德軍防禦使，在西北邊累立奇效。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yanzhou and defensive commissioner of the Tiande Army, repeatedly achieving extraordinary merit on the northwest frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Yanzhou and defensive commissioner of the Tiande Army, winning repeated extraordinary victories on the northwest frontier.

sentences.zh: 太和末，河西党項羌叛。

translations.literal: At the end of Taihe, the Tangut Qiang of Hexi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taihe era the Tangut Qiang of Hexi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 沔以天德之師屢誅其酋渠，移授振武節度使，檢校右散騎常侍、單於大都護。

translations.literal: Mian repeatedly destroyed their chieftains with Tiande forces; he was transferred and made military governor of Zhenwu, acting Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Protector of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: With the Tiande army Mian repeatedly killed their chieftains. He was transferred to serve as military governor of Zhenwu, acting Right Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Chief Protector of the Chanyu Protectorate.

sentences.zh: 開成中，党項雜虜大擾河西。

translations.literal: In the Kaicheng era, Tangut and various barbarians greatly harassed Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaicheng era Tangut and other frontier peoples greatly ravaged Hexi.

sentences.zh: 沔率吐渾、契苾、沙陁三部落等諸族萬人、馬三千騎，徑至銀、夏討襲，大破之。

translations.literal: Mian led ten thousand men from the Tuyuhun, Qibi, Shatuo and other tribes, with three thousand horses, directly to Yin and Xia to campaign and raid, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Mian led ten thousand men from the Tuyuhun, Qibi, Shatuo, and other allied tribes, with three thousand horsemen, straight into Yin and Xia to strike and raid, inflicting a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 俘獲萬計，告捷而還。

translations.literal: Captives and booty numbered in the tens of thousands; he reported victory and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Captives and booty numbered in the tens of thousands. He reported victory and returned.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校戶部尚書。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was further made acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was further made acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，回紇部饑，烏介可汗奉太和公主至漢南求食。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huichang, the Uyghur tribes suffered famine; Khan Wujie led Princess Taihe south of the Han frontier to seek provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huichang era the Uyghur tribes suffered famine. Khan Wujie led Princess Taihe south of the frontier to seek food.

sentences.zh: 過杷頭峰，犯雲、朔、北川。

translations.literal: Passing Potou Peak, they violated Yun, Shuo, and northern Bing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Potou Peak, they raided Yun, Shuo, and northern Bing.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以太原重地，控扼諸戎，乃移沔河東節度使、檢校尚書左僕射、太原尹、北京留守。

translations.literal: The court, considering Taiyuan a critical position controlling the various frontier peoples, transferred Mian to military governor of Hedong, acting Left Vice Director, Taiyuan Prefect, and Northern Capital Protector.
translations.idiomatic: The court, judging Taiyuan a vital strongpoint controlling the frontier peoples, transferred Mian to military governor of Hedong, acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, prefect of Taiyuan, and Protector of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 詔與幽州張仲武協力招撫回鶻，竟破虜寇，迎公主還宮。

translations.literal: He was ordered to join forces with Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou to pacify and win over the Uyghurs; they ultimately shattered the barbarian raiders and escorted the princess back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Zhang Zhongwu of Youzhou in winning over the Uyghurs by force and persuasion. In the end they broke the invaders and escorted the princess back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 以功進位檢校司空，尋改滑州刺史、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: For this achievement he was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works; soon after he was changed to prefect of Hua prefecture and military governor of the Yicheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was promoted to acting Grand Master of Works. Soon afterward he was reassigned as prefect of Hua and military governor of the Yicheng Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，潞帥劉從諫卒，子稹匿喪，擅主留務，要求旌鉞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the military commissioner of Lu, Liu Congjian, died. His son Zhen concealed the death, unilaterally assumed control of administrative affairs, and demanded the battle-axes of command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Liu Congjian, military commissioner of Lu, died. His son Zhen hid the death, seized control of the circuit on his own authority, and demanded the imperial battle-axes that would confirm his command.

sentences.zh: 武宗怒，命忠武節度使王宰、徐州節度李彥佐等，充潞府西南面招撫使。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong was enraged and ordered Wang Zai, military commissioner of Zhongwu, Li Yanzuo, military commissioner of Xuzhou, and others to serve as pacification commissioners for the southwest face of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Emperor Wuzong appointed Wang Zai of Zhongwu, Li Yanzuo of Xuzhou, and others as pacification commissioners for the southwestern approach to Lu.

sentences.zh: 遂復授沔太原節度，充潞府北面招討使。

translations.literal: Mian was then reappointed military commissioner of Taiyuan and assigned as punitive commissioner for the northern face of Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was then restored as military commissioner of Taiyuan and made punitive commissioner for the northern approach to Lu.

sentences.zh: 沔與張仲武不協，方征兵幽州，乃移沔為鄭滑節度使，進位檢校司徒。

translations.literal: Mian did not get along with Zhang Zhongwu. As troops were being raised in Youzhou, Mian was transferred to be military commissioner of Zheng-Hua and promoted to acting grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Mian and Zhang Zhongwu were at odds. While the court was raising troops in Youzhou, Mian was transferred to command Zheng-Hua and promoted to acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 既而以疾求歸洛陽，授太子太保，卒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, citing illness, he requested to return to Luoyang. He was appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, pleading illness, he asked to retire to Luoyang. He was named grand preceptor of the heir apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 初，沔為忠武小校，從李光顏討淮西，為捉生將。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mian had been a junior officer in Zhongwu. He followed Li Guangyan in the campaign against Huaidong and served as a capture-alive officer.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Mian was a junior officer in Zhongwu. He followed Li Guangyan against Huaidong and served as a capture-alive officer.

sentences.zh: 前後遇賊血戰，鋒刃所傷，幾死者數四。

translations.literal: Time and again he met the enemy in bloody combat. Wounded by blade and point, he came within a hair's breadth of death on four occasions.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he fought the enemy hand to hand. Cut by blade and point, he nearly died four separate times.

sentences.zh: 嘗傷重臥草中，月黑不知歸路，昏然而睡，夢人授之雙燭，曰：「子方大貴，此行無患，可持此而還。」

translations.literal: Once, severely wounded, he lay in the grass. The moon was dark and he could not find the road back. Drowsy, he fell asleep. In a dream a man handed him twin candles and said: "Great honor awaits you. This journey holds no peril. Take these and return."
translations.idiomatic: Once, badly wounded, he lay hidden in the grass. The moon was black and he had lost the road home. He drifted into sleep, and in a dream a man gave him two candles, saying, "You are destined for greatness. This journey will not harm you. Take these and go back."

sentences.zh: 既行，炯然有雙光在前。

translations.literal: When he set out, two bright lights gleamed before him.
translations.idiomatic: When he went on, two bright lights shone ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 自後破虜危難，每行常有此光。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever he broke the enemy in danger and hardship, these twin lights always shone as he marched.
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever he broke through the enemy in peril, the twin lights appeared before him on the march.

sentences.zh: 及罷鎮後，雙光息。

translations.literal: After he was removed from his command, the twin lights vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was stripped of his command, the twin lights disappeared.

sentences.zh: 五年，李德裕出鎮，罷沔為太子太保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Deyu left the capital for a posting. Mian was dismissed from his command and made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Li Deyu left the capital for a provincial posting, and Mian was removed from command and made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年，以太子太保致仕卒。

translations.literal: The next year he retired as grand preceptor of the heir apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired as grand preceptor of the heir apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 石雄，徐州牙校也。

translations.literal: Shi Xiong was a garrison officer of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiong was a garrison officer in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 王智興之討李同捷，以雄為石廂捉生兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhixing campaigned against Li Tongjie, he made Xiong commander of the Stone Flank capture-alive cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhixing marched against Li Tongjie, he appointed Xiong commander of the Stone Flank capture-alive cavalry.

sentences.zh: 勇敢善戰，氣淩三軍。

translations.literal: Bold and skilled in battle, his spirit towered over the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and formidable in battle, his presence dominated the entire army.

sentences.zh: 自智興以兵臨賊境，率先收棣州，雄先驅渡河，前無堅陣。

translations.literal: From the time Zhixing led his army to the enemy border and was first to recover Di Prefecture, Xiong as vanguard crossed the river. No solid formation stood before him.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment Zhixing brought his army to the rebel frontier and took Di Prefecture first, Xiong led the vanguard across the river and no enemy line could hold him.

sentences.zh: 徐人伏雄之撫待，惡智興之虐，欲逐之而立雄。

translations.literal: The men of Xuzhou admired Xiong's care and kindness and hated Zhixing's cruelty. They wished to drive Zhixing out and install Xiong in his place.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers of Xuzhou loved Xiong for his kindness and hated Zhixing for his brutality. They wanted to oust Zhixing and put Xiong in command.

sentences.zh: 智興以軍在賊境，懼其變生，因其立功，請授一郡刺史。

translations.literal: Zhixing, with the army deep in enemy territory, feared mutiny might erupt. Relying on Xiong's achievements, he requested that Xiong be granted a governorship in some prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With his army deep in enemy country, Zhixing feared a mutiny. Using Xiong's battlefield record as pretext, he asked the court to give Xiong a prefectural governorship.

sentences.zh: 朝廷征赴京師，授壁州刺史。

translations.literal: The court summoned him to the capital and appointed him governor of Bizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him to the capital and appointed him governor of Bizhou.

sentences.zh: 智興尋殺雄之素相善諸將士百余人，仍奏雄搖動軍情，請行誅戮。

translations.literal: Zhixing soon killed more than a hundred officers and soldiers who had been on good terms with Xiong, and memorialized that Xiong had shaken army morale, requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixing then slaughtered more than a hundred officers and men who had been close to Xiong, and reported that Xiong had undermined army morale, asking that he be put to death.

sentences.zh: 文宗雅知其能，惜之，乃長流白州。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong had long valued his ability and was loath to lose him. He was therefore exiled afar to Baizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had long known his worth and was reluctant to destroy him, so he was exiled to distant Baizhou instead.

sentences.zh: 太和中，河西党項擾亂，選求武士。

translations.literal: In the Tahe reign era, the Tangut tribes west of the Yellow River caused unrest, and the court sought out martial men.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tahe era, Tangut unrest broke out west of the river, and the court went looking for fighting men.

sentences.zh: 乃召還，隸振武劉沔軍為裨將，累立破羌之功。

translations.literal: He was recalled and attached to Liu Mian's Zhenwu army as a deputy general, repeatedly winning victories in campaigns against the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and placed under Liu Mian in the Zhenwu army as a deputy commander, winning repeated victories over the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 文宗以智興故，未甚提擢，而李紳、李德裕以崔群舊將，素嘉之。

translations.literal: Because of Zhixing, Emperor Wenzong did not promote him greatly. But Li Shen and Li Deyu, as former associates of Cui Qun, had long admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Zhixing, Emperor Wenzong did not advance him far, though Li Shen and Li Deyu, both old associates of Cui Qun, had admired him for years.

sentences.zh: 會昌初，回鶻寇天德，詔命劉沔為招撫回鶻使。

translations.literal: At the start of Huichang, the Uyghurs raided Tiande. An edict appointed Liu Mian commissioner for pacifying the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Huichang era the Uyghurs raided Tiande, and Liu Mian was appointed commissioner for pacifying the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 三年，回鶻大掠雲、朔北邊，牙於五原。

translations.literal: In the third year the Uyghurs looted heavily along the northern borders of Yun and Shuo and established their headquarters at Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the Uyghurs ravaged the northern borders of Yun and Shuo and made their camp at Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 沔以太原之師屯於雲州。

translations.literal: Mian encamped the Taiyuan army at Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mian stationed the Taiyuan army at Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 沔謂雄曰：「黠虜離散，不足驅除。

translations.literal: Mian said to Xiong: "These cunning barbarians are scattered. They are not worth a full drive to expel.
translations.idiomatic: Mian told Xiong, "These cunning barbarians are scattered and hardly worth a full campaign to drive off.

sentences.zh: 國家以公主之故，不欲急攻。

translations.literal: Because of the Princess, the state does not wish to press the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the princess, the court does not want to attack in force.

sentences.zh: 今觀其所為，氣淩我輩。

translations.literal: But seeing how they act now, their arrogance towers over us.
translations.idiomatic: Yet look at what they are doing now—they treat us with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 若稟朝旨，或恐依違。

translations.literal: If we seek instruction from the court, we may well be met with hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for orders from the capital, we may only get delay and indecision.

sentences.zh: 我輩捍邊，但能除患，專之可也。

translations.literal: We who defend the border need only remove the danger. We may decide on our own.
translations.idiomatic: Our duty on the frontier is to remove the threat. We can decide this ourselves.

sentences.zh: 公可選驍健，乘其不意，徑趨虜帳，彼以疾雷之勢，不暇枝梧，必棄公主亡竄。

translations.literal: You should choose the fiercest warriors and, catching them unawares, strike straight at their camp. Struck like thunder they will have no time to brace themselves and will abandon the Princess and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Choose your best fighters, take them by surprise, and strike straight at their camp. Hit them like thunder and they will not have time to brace themselves—they will abandon the princess and run.

sentences.zh: 事茍不捷，吾自繼進，亦無患也。」

translations.literal: If the plan fails, I will follow up myself. There is no cause for worry."
translations.idiomatic: If it fails, I will come up behind you myself. There is nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 雄受教，自選勁騎，得沙陁李國昌三部落，兼契苾拓拔雜虜三千騎，月暗夜發馬邑，徑趨烏介之牙。

translations.literal: Xiong accepted the plan. He personally selected crack horsemen—three clans of the Shatuo under Li Guochang, together with three thousand mixed barbarian riders of the Qibi and Toba—and set out from Mayi on a moonless night, driving straight for Wujie's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong took the order. He picked elite cavalry himself—three Shatuo clans under Li Guochang, plus three thousand Qibi, Toba, and other allied riders—and on a moonless night marched out of Mayi straight for Wujie's camp.

sentences.zh: 時虜帳逼振武，雄既入城，登堞視其眾寡。

translations.literal: The barbarian camp then pressed close to Zhenwu. Xiong entered the city and mounted the battlements to gauge their numbers.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarian camp was then pressing on Zhenwu. Xiong entered the city and climbed the wall to count their strength.

sentences.zh: 見氈車數十，從者皆衣硃碧，類華人服飾。

translations.literal: He saw several dozen felt-wheeled carts. Their attendants all wore cinnabar and azure, like Chinese dress.
translations.idiomatic: He saw several dozen felt-wheeled carts, their attendants dressed in red and green like Chinese servants.

sentences.zh: 雄令諜者訊之：「此何大人？」

translations.literal: Xiong sent a scout to inquire: "Whose pavilion is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiong sent a spy to ask, "Whose tent is that?"

sentences.zh: 虜曰：「此公主帳也。」

translations.literal: The barbarians answered: "This is the Princess's pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians replied, "That is the princess's tent."

sentences.zh: 雄喻其人曰：「國家兵馬欲取可汗。

translations.literal: Xiong instructed the man: "The state's troops mean to take the khan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong told the man, "The imperial army is coming for the khan.

sentences.zh: 公主至此，家國也，須謀歸路。

translations.literal: The Princess has reached this place. It is her native land, and a way home must be found.
translations.idiomatic: The princess has come home to her own country. She must be given a road back.

sentences.zh: 俟兵合時不得動帳幕。」

translations.literal: When the armies join battle, do not move the pavilion."
translations.idiomatic: When the fighting begins, do not move her tent."

sentences.zh: 雄乃大率城內牛馬雜畜及大鼓，夜穴城為十余門。

translations.literal: Xiong then gathered all cattle, horses, and mixed livestock within the city, plus great drums. By night he dug more than ten gates through the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong then rounded up every ox, horse, and beast in the city, along with great drums, and by night broke more than ten gates through the wall.

sentences.zh: 遲明，城上立旗幟炬火，乃於諸門縱其牛畜，鼓噪從之，直犯烏介牙帳。

translations.literal: At dawn banners and torches rose on the walls. From each gate he released the cattle and livestock, with drums and clamor following, and charged straight at Wujie's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak banners and torches went up on the walls. From every gate he turned the livestock loose, drums roaring behind them, and drove straight at Wujie's camp.

sentences.zh: 炬火燭天，鼓噪動地，可汗惶駭莫測，率騎而奔。

translations.literal: Torches lit the sky. Drums and shouts shook the earth. The khan was terrified beyond measure and fled with his horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Torches blazed across the sky and the din shook the ground. The khan, terrified out of his wits, fled with his riders.

sentences.zh: 雄率勁騎追至殺胡山，急擊之。

translations.literal: Xiong led his crack cavalry in pursuit to Mount Shahu and pressed the attack hard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong chased him with elite cavalry to Mount Shahu and struck hard.

sentences.zh: 斬首萬級，生擒五千，羊馬車帳皆委之而去。

translations.literal: They cut ten thousand heads, took five thousand alive, and abandoned sheep, horses, carts, and pavilions as they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They took ten thousand heads, captured five thousand alive, and left sheep, horses, carts, and tents behind as they withdrew.
