sentences.zh: 遂迎公主還太原。

translations.literal: They then escorted the Princess back to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Then they escorted the princess back to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 以功加檢校左散騎常侍、豐州刺名、兼御史大夫、天德防禦等使。

translations.literal: For his achievement he was promoted to acting left regular palace attendant, governor of Feng Prefecture, concurrent censor-in-chief, and commissioner of Tiande defense, among other posts.
translations.idiomatic: For this victory he was promoted to acting left regular palace attendant, governor of Feng Prefecture, concurrent censor-in-chief, and commissioner of Tiande defense, among other honors.

sentences.zh: 雄沈勇徇義，臨財甚廉。

translations.literal: Xiong was deep-thinking and brave, devoted to righteousness, and scrupulously honest when wealth passed his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong was thoughtful and resolute, devoted to duty, and scrupulously honest with money.

sentences.zh: 每破賊立功，朝廷特有賜與，皆不入私室；

translations.literal: Whenever he defeated the enemy and won merit, the special gifts the court sent him never entered his private quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he defeated the enemy and won merit, the special rewards the court sent never went into his private rooms.

sentences.zh: 置於軍門，首取一分，余並分給，以此軍士感義，皆思奮發。

translations.literal: He placed them at the army gate, took one share for himself first, and divided the rest among the men. For this the soldiers were moved by his righteousness and all burned to fight harder.
translations.idiomatic: He put them at the camp gate, took one share for himself, and handed out the rest. The men were moved by his fairness and fought all the harder for it.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校左僕射、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to acting left vice premier, prefect of Hezhong, and military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to acting left vice premier, prefect of Hezhong, and military commissioner of Hezhong-Jin-Jiang.

sentences.zh: 俄而昭義劉從諫卒，其子稹擅主軍務，朝議問罪。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died. His son Zhen seized control of military affairs, and court opinion called for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liu Congjian of Zhaoyi died. His son Zhen took command of the army on his own authority, and the court resolved to punish him.

sentences.zh: 令徐帥李彥佐為潞府西南面招撫使，以晉州刺史李丕為副。

translations.literal: Li Yanzuo, military commissioner of Xuzhou, was ordered to serve as pacification commissioner for the southwest face of Lu Prefecture, with Li Pi, governor of Jin Prefecture, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzuo of Xuzhou was made pacification commissioner for the southwestern approach to Lu, with Li Pi, governor of Jin Prefecture, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 時王宰在萬善柵，劉沔在石會，相顧未進。

translations.literal: Wang Zai was at Wanshan stockade and Liu Mian at Shihui. They looked at one another and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai held Wanshan stockade and Liu Mian was at Shihui. The two armies hung back and would not move.

sentences.zh: 雄受代之翌日，越烏嶺，破賊五砦，斬獲千計。

translations.literal: The day after Xiong accepted the transfer, he crossed Wuling, broke five enemy forts, and killed or captured more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Xiong took over the command, he crossed Wuling, smashed five rebel forts, and killed or captured more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 武宗聞捷大悅，謂侍臣曰：「今之義而有勇，罕有雄之比者。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, hearing of the victory, was greatly pleased and told his attendants: "Among those who combine righteousness with courage today, few can compare with Xiong."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong heard the news he was delighted and told his ministers, "Among the men of our day who combine righteousness with courage, few can match Xiong."

sentences.zh: 雄既率先破賊，不旬日，王宰收天井關，何弘敬、王元逵亦收磁洺等郡。

translations.literal: Once Xiong had been first to break the enemy, within ten days Wang Zai took Tianjing Pass, and He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui also recovered Ci, Ming, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiong broke the rebels first, Wang Zai took Tianjing Pass within ten days, and He Hongjing and Wang Yuankui recovered Ci, Ming, and the other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先是潞州狂人折腰於市，謂人曰：「雄七千人至矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier a madman in Lu Prefecture had doubled over in the marketplace and told people: "Xiong and seven thousand men are coming."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a madman in Lu had bent double in the marketplace and cried out, "Xiong and seven thousand men are coming!"

sentences.zh: 劉從諫捕而誅之。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian had him seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian had him arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 及稹危蹙，大將郭誼密款請斬稹歸朝，軍中疑其詐。

translations.literal: When Zhen was pressed to desperation, the great general Guo Yi secretly pledged to behead Zhen and surrender to the court. The army suspected treachery.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhen was cornered, the senior general Guo Yi secretly offered to kill Zhen and surrender to the court, but the army suspected a trick.

sentences.zh: 雄倡言曰：「賊稹之叛，郭誼為謀主。

translations.literal: Xiong spoke up publicly: "In Zhen the traitor's rebellion, Guo Yi was the chief plotter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong declared openly, "Guo Yi was the chief architect of Zhen's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 今請斬稹，即誼自謀，又何疑焉？」

translations.literal: Now he asks to behead Zhen. That is his own scheme. What is there to doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Now he offers to kill Zhen—that is his own design. Why should we doubt him?"

sentences.zh: 武宗亦以狂人之言，詔雄以七千兵受降。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong, also recalling the madman's words, ordered Xiong to accept the surrender with seven thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong, remembering the madman's prophecy as well, ordered Xiong to accept the surrender with seven thousand men.

sentences.zh: 雄即徑馳潞州降誼，盡擒其黨與。

translations.literal: Xiong rode straight to Lu Prefecture, accepted Yi's surrender, and captured all his accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong rode straight to Lu, accepted Yi's surrender, and seized all his followers.

sentences.zh: 賊平，進加檢校司空。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he was further promoted to acting minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion was crushed, he was further promoted to acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 王宰，智興之子，於雄不足，雄以轅門子弟善禮之。

translations.literal: Wang Zai was Zhixing's son. Though he fell short of Xiong in stature, Xiong treated him courteously as a scion of the military gates.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zai was Zhixing's son and no match for Xiong in ability, yet Xiong treated him with courtesy as a fellow soldier's son.

sentences.zh: 然討潞之役，雄有始卒之功，宰心惡之。

translations.literal: Yet in the Lu campaign Xiong had merit from first to last, and Zai resented him in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: But in the Lu campaign Xiong had done the decisive work from start to finish, and Zai hated him for it.

sentences.zh: 及李德裕罷相，宰黨排擯雄，罷鎮。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu was removed as chief minister, Zai's faction pushed Xiong aside and stripped him of his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu fell from power, Zai's faction forced Xiong out and stripped him of his command.

sentences.zh: 既而聞德裕貶，發疾而卒。

translations.literal: Not long after, upon hearing that Deyu had been demoted, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, on hearing that Deyu had been banished, he took ill and died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古所謂名將者，不必蒙輪拔距之材，拉虎批熊之力；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: What ancients called a famous general did not require the talent to hide under chariot wheels and wrestle at spear's length, nor the strength to drag tigers and smite bears.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The great generals of old were not necessarily men who could crouch beneath chariot wheels or outjump a spear-throw, nor men with the brute strength to wrestle tigers and bears.

sentences.zh: 要當以義終始，好謀而成。

translations.literal: What mattered was to begin and end in righteousness and achieve victory through sound planning.
translations.idiomatic: What mattered was to keep faith from first to last and win through careful planning.

sentences.zh: 而阿跌昆仲，稟氣陰山，率多令範。

translations.literal: Among the Adie brothers, nurtured by the spirit of the Yin Mountains, most lived up to fine examples.
translations.idiomatic: The Adie brothers, bred in the shadow of the Yin Mountains, mostly lived up to noble example.

sentences.zh: 讓家權於主婦，拒美妓於奸臣；

translations.literal: They yielded household authority to the lady of the house and refused beauteous musicians from treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: They yielded household authority to their wives and refused the gift of courtesans from corrupt ministers.

sentences.zh: 章武恢復之功，義師之效也。

translations.literal: Zhangwu's achievement in restoration was the work of righteous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration won under Emperor Wuzong was the fruit of righteous soldiery.

sentences.zh: 重胤忠於事上，仁於撫下，淮、蔡之役，勛亞光顏；

translations.literal: Chongyin was loyal in serving his superiors and humane in caring for those below. In the Huai-Cai campaign his merit ranked second only to Guangyan.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin was loyal to his superiors and humane toward his men. In the Huai-Cai campaign his merit stood second only to Guangyan's.

sentences.zh: 殿邦之臣也，不可多得。

translations.literal: Such pillars of the realm are not easily found in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Men who truly stabilize the realm are not easily found.

sentences.zh: 王沛之擒僚婿，李祐之執賊渠，皆因事立功，轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Wang Pei's capture of his son-in-law among the rebels and Li You's seizure of the rebel ringleader both turned circumstance to merit and transformed calamity into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei seized his rebel son-in-law and Li You captured the rebel chieftain—both turned accident into achievement and disaster into reward.

sentences.zh: 智則智矣，仁者不為！

translations.literal: Clever, yes—but a man of benevolence would not do such things!
translations.idiomatic: Clever they were—but a man of true humanity would not have done such things!

sentences.zh: 而劉悟自恃太尤，世邀纘襲，至於赤族，報亦晚耶！

translations.literal: Yet Liu Wu, trusting overmuch in himself and generation after generation grasping at inherited command, brought annihilation upon his entire clan. Is not the reckoning overdue?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Wu, swollen with pride and grasping at hereditary command generation after generation, brought extinction on his whole house—was not the reckoning long overdue?

sentences.zh: 雄、沔負羽邊城，聲馳沙漠，奉迎貴主，摧破昆戎，不亦壯乎！

translations.literal: Xiong and Mian bore arms on the frontier. Their fame raced across the desert. They welcomed home a noble princess and shattered the barbarian hordes. Is this not glorious?
translations.idiomatic: Xiong and Mian carried the frontier on their shoulders, their fame ringing across the desert; they brought home a princess and broke the northern tribes—what could be more glorious?

sentences.zh: 雄能感於知己，不為無義，美哉！

translations.literal: That Xiong could be moved by those who truly knew him and would not betray righteousness—how fine!
translations.idiomatic: That Xiong could repay those who believed in him and would not abandon righteousness—how admirable!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：淮、鄆砥平，義將輸誠。

translations.literal: The encomium says: When Huai and Yun were leveled flat, righteous generals offered their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: When Huai and Yan were pacified, loyal generals gave their allegiance.

sentences.zh: 二兇受縛，亦其同惡。

translations.literal: When the two villains were bound, their accomplices in evil shared their fate.
translations.idiomatic: When the two villains were taken, their fellow conspirators shared their doom.

sentences.zh: 毀義棄忠，必殄爾宗。

translations.literal: Destroy righteousness and abandon loyalty, and your clan will surely be wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Break faith and cast aside loyalty, and your house will be destroyed to the last man.

sentences.zh: 孰稱善將？

translations.literal: Who may be called a good general?
translations.idiomatic: Who deserves to be called a true general?

sentences.zh: 劉沔、石雄。

translations.literal: Liu Mian and Shi Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian and Shi Xiong.
